B. Braun Medical Inc., a leader in infusion therapy and pain management, develops, manufactures, and markets innovative medical products and services to the healthcare industry. Other key product areas include nutrition, pharmacy admixture and compounding, ostomy and wound care, and dialysis. The company is committed to eliminating preventable treatment errors and enhancing patient, clinician and environmental safety. B. Braun Medical is headquartered in Bethlehem, Pa., and is part of the B. Braun Group of Companies in the U.S., which includes B. Braun Interventional Systems, Aesculap® and CAPS®.

Globally, the B. Braun Group of Companies employs more than 64,000 employees in 64 countries. Guided by its Sharing Expertise® philosophy, B. Braun continuously exchanges knowledge with customers, partners and clinicians to address the critical issues of improving care and lowering costs. To learn more about B. Braun Medical, visit www.bbraunusa.com

Ready to lead where science, quality, and patient safety come together? Join B. Braun and shape the future of laboratory excellence while driving the strategy, compliance, and innovation behind critical healthcare products.

**Why this role matters:**

The Director, Lab Quality Control serves as the senior site authority for Quality Control Chemistry and Microbiology, providing the scientific and operational leadership needed to protect product quality and maintain regulatory compliance. This role establishes the site’s laboratory strategy, leads critical quality initiatives, and ensures that laboratory operations remain scientifically sound, inspection-ready, and aligned with business and product portfolio requirements.

**How you will make an impact:**

* Develop, maintain, and execute the site Quality Control strategy in alignment with business objectives, product portfolio requirements, and regulatory expectations.
* Provide strategic oversight for QC Chemistry and QC Microbiology operations, including release, stability, raw material, in-process, microbiological, and sterility-related testing activities.
* Establish and govern laboratory standards for testing compliance, data integrity, investigations, sample management, analytical methods, specifications, and laboratory workflows.
* Serve as the primary site subject matter expert during regulatory inspections and customer audits involving laboratory operations and quality systems.
* Partner with Quality Assurance, Manufacturing, Sterility Assurance, Engineering, Validation, Technical Services, Supply Chain, and Regulatory Affairs to support site operations and timely product release.
* Lead laboratory optimization, method modernization, automation, Lean deployment, and quality system improvement initiatives.
* Foster a culture of quality, accountability, scientific rigor, collaboration, safety, and continuous improvement.

**What sets you up for success:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline required; master’s degree or doctorate preferred.
* 10+ years of related experience, including significant leadership responsibility within laboratory quality control or pharmaceutical manufacturing.
* Demonstrated expertise in QC Chemistry and/or QC Microbiology operations within a sterile drug product manufacturing environment.
* Significant experience with laboratory compliance, data integrity, out-of-specification and out-of-trend investigations, analytical methods, and pharmaceutical quality systems.
* Proven experience supporting regulatory inspections, customer audits, and interactions with senior internal and external stakeholders.
* Ability to resolve complex scientific, operational, and compliance issues using sound judgment, technical expertise, and risk-based decision-making.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or demonstrated experience applying Lean and continuous-improvement methodologies preferred.

**What you will enjoy along the way:**

* The opportunity to shape the laboratory quality strategy for a regulated sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing site.
* A highly visible leadership role with influence across Quality, Manufacturing, Technical Operations, Supply Chain, and Regulatory Affairs.
* The ability to modernize analytical capabilities through automation, method lifecycle management, Lean principles, and emerging technologies.
* Responsibility for developing laboratory leaders, building organizational capability, and determining the effective allocation of people and resources.
* Meaningful work that directly supports product quality, regulatory compliance, operational reliability, and patient safety.
* A collaborative environment built on scientific rigor, accountability, diverse perspectives, and continuous improvement.

Salary Range: $184,000 - $261,000

existing_roles.title: Director, United States Operations Quality Audits & Inspections
existing_roles.description:
Facility: Quality

Location:
Plainsboro, NJ, US

**About the Department**

 

The Clinical, Medical and Regulatory (CMR) department at Novo Nordisk is one of the most diverse and collaborative groups within the organization. From healthcare provider interactions and developing and implementing regulatory strategies with the FDA to providing medical education and collecting data to support efficacy and new product development, CMR is involved. The one thing that keeps us all marching to the same beat is our patient centered focus. At Novo Nordisk, you will help patients around the world. As their needs evolve, so does our challenge to find better and more innovative ways to improve their quality of life. We’re changing lives for a living. Are you ready to make a difference?

 

**The Position**

Lead independent, risk-based quality audits and inspection readiness across the approved USO Quality (USOQ) domain. Develop and execute the audit and self-inspection strategy to assess compliance, control effectiveness and risks to patient safety, product quality and data integrity across applicable current GxPs [Good Clinical (GCP), Pharmacovigilance (GPV), Distribution (GDP) and Manufacturing (GMP)] practices]. Maintain an objective view of business and Quality activities, including outsourced activities within scope. Lead sustained audit and inspection readiness and act as the designated local health authority inspection point of contact and inspection lead for the USOQ domain, coordinating with Regulatory Affairs, Global Quality, Patient Safety and accountable business leaders. Ensure readiness gaps and regulatory commitments are visible, owned, and escalated. Provide independent assurance over external-party quality controls through risk-based audits & remediation plans.

 

**Relationships**

Position reports to the Head of USO Quality. The sponsor approves the audit charter and risk-based plan, reviews resource adequacy, receives unfiltered findings and has formal input into the Director’s appointment, removal and performance assessment. The Director has direct access to the sponsor to escalate interference, disputed findings, scope restrictions and unresolved material risks. Interface with multiple Novo accountable business leaders, Regulatory Affairs, Legal, Safety, global Quality Audit and Global Clinical Compliance. External relationships include health authorities, clinical trial sites, external auditors and relevant vendors and partners. Coordinate USOQ inspection communications through approved authority channels without displacing global, legal-entity, Regulatory or Safety accountabilities. This role manages the independent audit and inspection department, with multiple experienced quality representatives assigned to diverse quality functions and includes auditor competence, inspection leadership, workload, budget and continuity.

 

**Essential Functions**

* Direct Independent Audits and Self-Inspection Program & Staff
* Maintain the USOQ audit charter, audit universe and risk-based audit and self-inspection strategy. Define scope, frequency, methods, auditor qualifications and escalation criteria across business functions, Quality verticals and relevant external parties. Secure approval of audit plans and material changes, ensure authorized access to personnel, sites, systems and records and align with global audit programs to prevent duplication and coverage gaps
* Lead the annual audit & self-inspection program, including routine, risk-triggered and for-cause reviews. Assign qualified, independent auditors; oversee evidence-based assessments of control design, effectiveness, data integrity and external-party controls. Ensure consistent finding classification, clear communication and timely reporting. Manage budget and staffing, document plan deviations and escalate material coverage or resource gaps
* Inspection Readiness and Health Authority Leadership
* Lead inspection readiness with business and Quality leaders through assessments, mock inspections, playbooks, document-retrieval exercises, SME preparation and trained deputies. Define inspection-team roles, front- and back-room responsibilities, request tracking and escalation. Coordinate USOQ administrative support while leading readiness coordination and independent challenge. Business and process owners retain responsibility for compliant operations, source records and readiness evidence
* Serve as the designated local health authority inspection contact and lead within approved USOQ scope, including FDA and other formally assigned authorities. Coordinate inspection logistics, meetings, interviews, requests and communications with Regulatory Affairs, global functions and accountable SMEs. Lead observation triage, response coordination and commitment tracking. Secure authorized approvals for submissions, commitments and risk acceptance; retain established company signatory, Regulatory and Safety reporting authorities
* Finding Ownership and Remediation Oversight
* Ensure all audit, self-inspection and inspection findings have accountable business or process owners, action owners, deadlines and escalation routes. Business leaders assign ownership and resources; finding owners investigate root causes, develop and implement CAPA and demonstrate effectiveness. Quality owns findings within its processes. Challenge inadequate responses and escalate unassigned, overdue, repeat or high-risk findings to the Head of USOQ and Corporate Quality Audit Sponsor, as appropriate. Honor health authority deadlines
* Independently assess audit and self-inspection responses and verify remediation effectiveness before closing findings under approved procedures. Require additional evidence or action where needed. For inspection observations, coordinate completion and effectiveness checks while preserving authorized response approvals and health authority closure decisions. Reviewers must not assess their own remediation; finding owners retain investigation, CAPA development and implementation
* Report audit themes, inspection readiness, overdue commitments and systemic risks to the Quality Council and relevant global forums. Escalate urgent risks immediately and independence concerns directly to the Corporate Quality Audit Sponsor
* Independence and Performance
* Protect audit objectivity through a documented charter, conflict disclosures, independent assignments and unfiltered reporting. Base conclusions on evidence, free from business or delivery pressures; escalate classification disputes through approved independent channels. Do not operate or approve controls the team audits; arrange independent review of its readiness and inspection-coordination activities. Track risk-based coverage, reporting and regulatory-response timeliness, readiness-gap closure, overdue and repeat findings, CAPA effectiveness and auditor competence. Do not incentivize low finding counts or guarantee inspection outcomes.
 

**Physical Requirements**

10-20% overnight travel required. This position (in-office) is located in Plainsboro, NJ.

 

**Development Of People**

Supervisory. Ensure that reporting personnel have individual development plans (IDP), with annual goals and measurements that are consistent with the priorities of the business and that interim reviews are held so that their work is focused on those priorities and they understand their level of accountability for results and the measurement process. Ensure that the IDP forms include completed learning and aspiration plans and are in place for all reporting personnel to enable the achievement of goals and capability to assume increased levels of responsibility. Manage the application and communication of all Novo Nordisk policies, procedures and Novo Nordisk Way.

 

**Qualifications**

* **Education level:** Bachelor’s degree required. Advanced degree preferred; advanced degree may substitute for 2 years of experience
* **Experience Level:** 10+ years of progressive experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or CRO industry, including at least 5 years in GxP Quality Assurance, Compliance, or related functions, and 5 years in people leadership or leading complex cross-functional quality initiatives. Demonstrated experience in commercial/affiliate quality, pharmacovigilance quality, regulatory inspections, and pharmaceutical Quality Management Systems (QMS). Broader GDP/GMP experience preferred.
* **Specific or technical job skills:** Deep expertise in GxP and FDA inspections; working knowledge of GPV/GDP/GMP/GCP and other requirements applicable to commercial & post-marketing operations. Demonstrated leadership of independent audits, self-inspection programs, inspection readiness and health authority inspections, including finding classification, root-cause/CAPA challenge and effectiveness verification. Ability to distinguish inspection coordination from business execution and authorized regulatory commitments 
 The base compensation range for this position is $187,100K to $327,000K. Base compensation is determined based on a number of factors. This position is also eligible for a company bonus based on individual and company performance. Novo Nordisk offers long-term incentive compensation and or company vehicles depending on the position's level or other company factors.

Employees are also eligible to participate in Company employee benefit programs including medical, dental and vision coverage; life insurance; disability insurance; 401(k) savings plan; flexible spending accounts; employee assistance program; tuition reimbursement program; and voluntary benefits such as group legal, critical illness, identity theft protection, pet insurance and auto/home insurance. The Company also offers time off pursuant to its sick time policy, flex-able vacation policy, and parental leave policy.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

 

At Novo Nordisk, we're not chasing quick fixes – we're creating lasting change for long-term health. For over 100 years, we've been driven by a single purpose: to defeat serious chronic diseases and help millions of people live healthier lives. This dedication fuels our constant curiosity and inspires us to push the boundaries of what's possible in healthcare. We embrace diverse perspectives, seek out bold ideas, and build partnerships rooted in shared purpose. Together, we're making healthcare more accessible, treating and defeating diseases, and pioneering solutions that create change spanning generations. When you join us, you become part of something bigger – a legacy of impact that reaches far beyond today.

 

Novo Nordisk is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by local, state or federal laws, rules or regulations.

 

If you are interested in applying to Novo Nordisk and need special assistance or an accommodation to apply, please call us at 1-855-411-5290. This contact is for accommodation requests only and cannot be used to inquire about the status of applications.

existing_roles.description:
Job Description
 
 
Position Overview
 
 
Quality Lead, Director– QMS & Digital Quality Governance Analytical
 
Global Quality Management Systems
 
 
The Global Quality Group within our Company Manufacturing Division is seeking an experienced transformation lead in the capacity of Director– Quality Management Systems (QMS) & Digital Quality Governance, to provide strategic and operational leadership for the QMS workstream within a complex, enterprise-level laboratory transformation program.
 
 
This role is accountable for architecting, modernizing, and deploying a modernized, digitized Quality Management System tailored to support next-generation QC testing, end-to-end analytical digitization, instrumentation innovation, and laboratory automation.
 
 
The QMS Quality Lead will oversee the harmonization and evolution of quality processes—including deviation management, investigations, CAPA, change control, risk management (ICH Q9), and computerized systems validation (CSV/CSA)—to ensure seamless integration with modern automated laboratory workflows, LIMS, ELN, and digital data pipelines. In close partnership with the program leadership team, Site Quality heads, Analytical Development, Digital/IT Quality, and Regulatory Compliance, the incumbent will ensure that innovative operational models maintain rigorous compliance with global health authority regulations while driving efficiency, inspection readiness, and continuous improvement.
 
 
Key Responsibilities and Requirements
 
The ideal candidate will combine deep technical expertise in global Quality Management Systems with a forward-thinking innovation mindset, translating digital and automated laboratory advancements into agile, compliant, and sustainable QMS frameworks.
 
 

* Strategic QMS Architecture & Modernization: Define, lead, and execute the QMS integration strategy for the lab transformation initiative, ensuring core quality processes (Change Control, OOS/OOE/OOT investigations, Deviations, CAPA, Method Transfer/Validation, and Batch Release support) are optimized, digitized, and natively integrated with automated laboratory systems
* Coding Experience: Experience and understanding on how coding translates to QMS and analytical functions. Responsible for overseeing the eQMS and ability to be able to review and understand the underlying code and how it is ensures compliance.
* Digital Quality & Data Integrity Governance: Partner with IT/Digital Quality and Automation engineers to embed robust Data Integrity by Design (ALCOA+) and Computer Software Assurance (CSA) principles into digitized laboratory platforms, instrument interfaces, and automated data flows.
* Regulatory Compliance & Inspection Readiness: Ensure all modernized QMS processes, policies, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) comply with global cGMP regulations (FDA 21 CFR Part 11/210/211, EU Annex 11, ICH Q9/Q10, WHO). Drive inspection readiness strategies and author/review corresponding regulatory briefing documents and filing sections.
* Matrixed Program Leadership & Governance: Direct the QMS workstream governance forum, actively tracking milestone execution, interdependencies, risks, and critical paths. Provide regular data-driven progress updates, risk assessments, and escalation pathways to the Overall Quality Lead and executive steering bodies.
* Change Management & Operational Transition: Drive human-centered change management and training initiatives to support site-level and global QC laboratory adoption of digitized quality workflows, fostering a strong culture of quality and transformation agent mindset.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Serve as the central quality authority across laboratory operations, technology development, computerized systems validation, and regulatory affairs, eliminating silos and resolving complex compliance roadblocks.
* People Leadership & Oversight: Supervise and mentor quality specialists, compliance leads, and external consultants supporting QMS transformation, maintaining high standards of technical rigor, accountability, and development.

Required Experience
 
 

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Pharmacy, Engineering, Life Sciences, or related discipline required; advanced degree (Master’s, PhD, PharmD, or MBA) strongly preferred.
* Experience: 10+ to 15+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical quality operations, quality systems, or compliance within a cGMP manufacturing and QC laboratory environment.
* Quality Systems Expertise: Proven track record in designing, optimizing, and overseeing enterprise-level QMS processes (Deviations, Investigations, CAPA, Change Control, Out of Specification, and Quality Risk Management) in laboratories subject to global health authority inspections (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA).
* Digital & Laboratory Systems Acumen: In-depth knowledge of laboratory digital ecosystems, including LIMS, ELN, CDS, SDMS, automated instrumentation, and their integration into enterprise QMS platforms (e.g., TrackWise, Veeva Vault QMS).
* Validation & Compliance Mastery: Strong understanding of Data Integrity expectations, 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, and modern risk-based validation methodologies (GAMP 5, Computer Software Assurance).
* Governance & Program Execution: Demonstrated success leading large-scale cross-functional workstreams, setting project milestones, proactively managing risk registers, and driving accountable execution.
* Communication & Influencing: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to present technical compliance strategies effectively to executive sponsors, auditors, and technical teams.

Preferred Experience
 
 

* Direct experience leading or supporting QMS transformation initiatives (e.g., transition from paper/hybrid to end-to-end digitized paperless QC environments).
* Working knowledge of automated testing platforms, robotics, or continuous manufacturing/testing control frameworks.
* Experience with global health authority inspections, pre-approval inspections (PAIs), and authoring QMS/Quality sections for regulatory dossiers (NDA, BLA, MAA).
* Practical application of Lean / Six Sigma methodologies to streamline quality workflows and cycle times.
* Programming experience is an asset, and or strong demonstrated ability to quickly learn.
* Experience supporting enterprise workforce strategy, technology evaluation, or transition initiatives.
* Experience managing external third party service providers, software vendors, and implementation partners in regulated environments.

**Required Skills:** 
Analytical Development, Cross-Functional Leadership, Digital Transformation, Enterprise Transformation, Executive Communications, GMP Compliance, Laboratory Quality Control, Project Governance, Quality Management Systems (QMS), Regulatory Strategies
 
 
**Preferred Skills:** 
Analytical Testing, Change Leadership, Program Governance

Summary
 
 
We are looking for a Director to build and lead the evaluation and quality assurance function for one of our most ambitious multi-year engineering initiatives. This is a true 0-to-1, first-key-hire role: There is no existing team, tooling, or process to inherit. You will define how we measure quality across an entire product end to end, build the automation and evaluation infrastructure to do it at scale (or borrow other teams' infrastructure), and build and lead the organization that runs it.
 
 
Description
 
 
You will own evaluation and quality assurance for every layer of the product — from whether the system is being correctly triggered for the right set of user requests, through whether it surfaces and ranks the right results, to whether the underlying transactions execute correctly, including integrations with external partner APIs, and financial systems. Quality here isn't a single test suite — it spans conversational understanding, relevance and ranking, and revenue-bearing correctness, all against a large, constantly evolving real-world dataset. You will create and drive the evaluation and quality strategy and implementation for the product. This will extensively utilize automated grading systems and human evaluation programs where appropriate. You will make the calls about where to invest in each. You will define what "correct" and "good" mean for this product, wire that definition into continuous, always-on evaluation pipelines with clear pass/fail quality gates tied to releases, and build the team, tooling, and operating rhythm to catch issues before they reach users. As the first hire in this space, you will operate with significant latitude and ambiguity — setting strategy, process, and technical direction with minimal existing scaffolding, while also building and scaling an organization. You will partner closely with engineering, applied ML, and program management leadership, including senior executive stakeholders, and you will be a key voice in defining what "done" and "shippable" mean for a product still taking shape, as well as iterating on decision points in production after the product ships.
 
 
Minimum Qualifications 
 
 

* 12+ years of experience in data science, machine learning evaluation, quality assurance, or test engineering roles in a technical product environment, including experience building and leading multi-level QA or evaluation organizations through managers.
* Demonstrated experience building an evaluation or QA function from the ground up — defining metrics, process, tooling, and organizational structure where none previously existed.
* Extensive experience utilizing LLM-based autograders and rubrics, including rubric design, evaluation set development, validation, calibration, and human-model alignment, and using them to proactively drive product and model improvements.
* Deep experience in traditional human evaluation methodology, logging, and A/B testing for consumer-facing products at scale.
* Experience evaluating conversational AI, recommendation, ranking, or search systems, and — ideally — agentic or tool-use systems that take real-world actions, not just generate responses.
* BS in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.
* Experience with quality assurance for third-party API integrations.
* Experience with logging infrastructure and instrumentation for AI product quality measurement.
* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of presenting quality status, risk, and trade-offs clearly to, and influencing decisions among, senior executive leadership.

 
 
 
Preferred Qualifications 
 
 

* 15+ years of experience in data science, machine learning evaluation, quality assurance, or test engineering roles in a technical product environment, including experience building and leading multi-level QA or evaluation organizations through managers.

existing_roles.title: Director, Quality
existing_roles.description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We’re looking for a Director, Quality to lead quality strategy and execution across Oura’s global engineering organization and supply chain.

### **What You Will Do:**

* In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
* You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
* This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
* Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
* Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
* Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
* Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
* Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
* Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
* Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
* Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
* Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.
* Lead launch and ramp readiness: Review product and component qualification, supplier capability, manufacturing readiness, validation evidence, yield, open risks, reliability results, and corrective actions before launch and ramp decisions.
* Govern quality-related changes: Ensure design, material, component, supplier, process, software, and manufacturing changes are evaluated for quality and reliability impact and implemented consistently through ECR/ECN and change-control processes.
* Establish a data-driven quality operating system: Define leading and lagging indicators across development, suppliers, manufacturing, and the field. Improve data quality, traceability, dashboards, and escalation mechanisms.
* Drive continuous improvement: Reduce defects, escapes, returns, warranty claims, rework, scrap, and other sources of cost of poor quality while improving product reliability, supplier performance, and customer experience.
* Influence cross-functional decisions: Provide clear, risk-based recommendations when quality, schedule, cost, performance, capacity, and supply continuity priorities compete.
* Communicate with senior leadership: Present concise assessments of product risk, supplier and manufacturing performance, launch readiness, field quality, and improvement priorities.
* Build a culture of prevention and accountability: Make quality a shared responsibility across engineering and operations, with clear ownership for requirements, validation, supplier controls, manufacturing execution, and sustained performance.

This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

### **What you'll bring**

* 15+ years of experience in product quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, operations quality, or a related engineering discipline, including significant people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success leading quality for complex, high-volume consumer electronics, wearable, medical-adjacent, or similarly reliability-sensitive products.
* Experience leading and developing teams across one or more of the following areas: product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, or sustaining quality.
* A track record of establishing quality strategy, operating mechanisms, and measurable improvements from early product development through launch and sustaining.
* Strong understanding of product development, design verification and validation, component qualification, reliability engineering, supplier quality, manufacturing processes, and production ramp.
* Strong command of quality and problem-solving methods, including FMEA, 8D, CAPA, SPC, GR&R, DOE, root-cause analysis, control plans, and process capability.
* Experience using engineering, field, warranty, customer support, supplier, and manufacturing data to identify systemic risks and drive corrective action.
* Demonstrated ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, and executive leadership without relying solely on direct authority.
* Experience with engineering change control, supplier changes, component qualification, process validation, manufacturing readiness, or production quality improvement.
* Strong understanding of DFM/DFA, GD&T, Lean and Six Sigma principles, measurement systems, and quality management systems.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical risks into concise decisions and actions.
* A self-directed, pragmatic, and resilient leadership style, with a willingness to engage deeply in details while maintaining a strategic perspective.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Systems, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field required; advanced degree or quality certification is a plus.
* Preferred qualifications
* Experience with both product quality and supplier or manufacturing quality, or demonstrated ability to operate effectively across both domains.
* Experience with batteries, electronics, sensors, RF systems, precision mechanics, adhesives, miniaturized assemblies, or other demanding product technologies.
* Experience leading quality for products that combine hardware, firmware, software, and cloud-enabled member experiences.
* Experience building or scaling quality management systems during rapid company growth.
* Familiarity with product safety, regulatory, compliance, traceability, and risk-management requirements relevant to wearable technology.
* Experience with supplier development, APQP, PPAP, SCAR processes, multi-source strategies, capacity expansion, or major manufacturing transitions.
* Experience working across multiple countries, engineering sites, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

### **Nice to have:**

* HW Experience
* Global distributor teams
* grown and org

### **Benefits**

At Ōura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Ōura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health.

What we offer:

* Competitive salary and equity packages
* Health, dental, vision insurance, and mental health resources
* An Ōura Ring of your own plus employee discounts for friends & family
* 20 days of paid time off plus 13 paid holidays plus 8 days of flexible wellness time off
* Paid sick leave and parental leave

Ōura takes a market-based approach to pay, which may vary depending on your location. US locations are categorized into tiers based on a cost of labor index for that geographic area. While most offers will be closer to the starting range, successful candidates' pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location, internal peer equity, and market conditions. These ranges may be modified in the future.

Region 1 $226,000-$266,000
 
Region 2 $MIN- $MID
 
Region 3 $MIN- $MID

A recruiter can determine your Region based on your US location.

We are not considering candidates residing in the following states: Alaska (AK), Delaware (DE), Iowa (IA), Mississippi (MS), Nebraska (NE), South Dakota (SD), West Virginia (WV), and Wisconsin (WI).

ŌURA is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Individuals seeking employment at ŌURA are considered without regard to age, ancestry, color, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, mental or physical disability, national origin, protected family care or medical leave status, race, religion (including beliefs and practices or the absence thereof), sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. We will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics.

We will work to ensure individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment.

Disclaimer: Beware of fake job offers!
 
We’ve been alerted to scammers posing as ŌURA recruiters, especially for remote roles. Please note:

* Our jobs are listed only on the ŌURA Careers page and trusted job boards.
* We will never ask for personal information like ID or payment for equipment upfront.
* Official offers are sent through Docusign after a verbal offer, not via text or email.

Stay cautious and protect your personal details.

To all recruitment agencies: ŌURA does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, ŌURA employees, or any other organization's location. ŌURA is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

Overview

:

**POSITION SUMMARY:** The Regional Director – Quality provides leadership for the assigned platforms’ clinical quality program. In partnership with physician leadership, the Regional Director – Quality supports clinical quality improvement, patient safety, clinician education, and quality governance. The Regional Director – Quality collaborates with facility partners, USAP’s data analytics team, and corporate leadership to advance quality initiatives and support physician-led clinical excellence.

Job Highlights

:

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**: (*The ideal candidate must be able to complete all physical requirements of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation)*

 

* Leads the platform's clinical quality program in collaboration with physician leadership.
* Supports implementation of local and enterprise quality initiatives.
* Identifies opportunities to improve clinical quality and patient safety.
* Coordinates platform participation in enterprise quality initiatives, as applicable.
* Manages the case review process in collaboration with the local Clinical Quality Committee (CQC).
* Reviews unexpected clinical outcomes, referrals, trends, and other quality concerns.
* Conducts review of clinical events and recommends opportunities for system or practice improvement.
* Escalates issues through established governance pathways, as appropriate.
* Facilitates the development and implementation of quality improvement initiatives.
* Evaluates the effectiveness of quality improvement initiatives.
* Shares best practices across platforms.
* Develops and coordinates clinician education arising from quality initiatives, patient safety activities, case reviews, and other clinically relevant topics identified by the platform CQC.
* Orients new clinicians to the platform’s quality program.
* Supports the development, implementation, and ongoing review of clinical protocols and practice guidelines in collaboration with physician leadership.
* Reviews patient satisfaction feedback and trends to identify opportunities to improve clinical quality and patient safety.
* Partners with the data analytics team to define quality reporting needs, including relevant dashboards.
* Identifies data-informed opportunities for improvement in collaboration with the platform CQC.
* Supports the platform CQC.
* Partners with facility quality and physician leaders to advance quality initiatives, including representing the platform on facility quality committees, as appropriate.
* Coordinates quality reporting required by facility and payor contracts and applicable regulatory agencies.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

:

**K****NOWLEDGE/SKILLS/ABILITIES** **(KSAs):**

 

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare or related field required, master’s degree preferred.
* 5+ years’ progressively responsible healthcare quality experience, preferably in a physician practice, ambulatory, or perioperative setting.
* Knowledge of quality improvement principles and patient safety.
* Knowledge of Power BI preferred.
* Knowledge of healthcare regulatory and accreditation requirements relevant to physician practice.
* Knowledge of clinical quality review methodologies and quality governance processes.
* Ability to interpret quality data and trends.
* Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills.
* Ability to lead and facilitate committee discussions and communicate complex information to diverse audiences.
* Ability to build collaborative relationships with clinicians, facility leaders, and multidisciplinary teams.
* Experience leading quality improvement initiatives across multiple sites.
* Demonstrated ability to influence through collaboration and trust building.
* Demonstrated commitment to professionalism, integrity, confidentiality, and continuous improvement.
* Experience leading, mentoring, and developing a high-performing team.

* *The physical demands described here are representative of those that may need to be met by an employee to successfully p**er**form the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.*

* *Occasional Standing*
* *Occasional Walking*
* *Frequent Sitting*
* *Frequent hand, finger movement*
* *Use office equipment (in office or remote)*
* *Communicate verbally and in writing*

existing_roles.title: Director, Quality & Compliance
existing_roles.description:
Overview:

As a perennial leader in health care in Florida, University of Florida Health Shands Hospital is once again recognized by the U.S. News & World Report’s Best Hospitals rankings for excellence in adult patient care, with seven medical specialties ranked among the nation’s elite. Combined with the five pediatric specialties ranked in the nation’s top 50 by U.S. News & World Report, UF Health Shands has 12 specialties recognized.

Responsibilities:

Develops and implements the Continuous Quality Improvement program; coordinates licensure and accreditation activities for compliance with all applicable regularly agencies; serves as risk manager designee and directs the risk management program; supports the Medical Directors; establishes and assures hospital standards of performance; provides ongoing administrative, utilization and clinical quality consultation and support to the educators, managers, administrator and medical director of UF Health Psychiatric Hospital and UF Health system. Manages cost centers, departments and projects as assigned. Conducts special projects and serves as hospital representative to related core and system teams, projects and initiatives. Serves as a member of the hospital senior management team; represents administration in the absence of the Administrator and participates actively in institutional decision making. Chair the Emergency Preparedness to coordinate disaster relief efforts with County and State emergency management officials. Participate in the administrative on-call rotation.

Qualifications:

**Education**

* Bachelor’s degree required.
* Master’s degree preferred.
* Master’s degree or higher in healthcare administration, risk management, nursing, or a directly applicable discipline preferred.

**Experience**

* Three to five years of progressively responsible management experience in a hospital setting, or equivalent, required.
* Experience with continuous quality improvement required.
* Experience with The Joint Commission accreditation required.
* Experience with Chapter 394 of the Florida Statutes, Rule 10E of the Florida Administrative Code, the Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA), and/or other applicable regulatory agencies preferred.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

* Demonstrated ability to organize and design services.
* Strong analytical skills.
* Demonstrated competency in:
* + Problem definition
 + Solution development
 + Issue resolution
 + Implementation
* Strong verbal and written communication skills.
* Strong conflict-resolution and conflict-management skills.
* Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects and initiatives.
* Knowledge of procedural terminology and healthcare systems.

**Motor Vehicle Operator Designation**

* Will operate vehicles for an assigned business purpose as a non-frequent driver.
* A frequent driver is defined as an employee who uses a personal or Shands vehicle:
* + At least once daily;
 + For at least five individual trips per week; or
 + To drive an average of more than 150 miles per week while performing job duties.
* The appropriate motor vehicle operator designation must be indicated on the Request for Personnel (RFP) form when the RFP is submitted to post the position.

**Licensure/Certification/Registration**

* None provided.

existing_roles.title: General Manager - Automotive Manufacturing
existing_roles.description:
"An Equal Opportunity Employer” It is the policy of North American Stamping Group to provide employment, training, promotion, and other conditions of Employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age or status as a qualified individual with a disability or other status protected by law.
 
 
GENERAL SUMMARY
 
Plans, advises, consults, leads, and coordinates manufacturing, manufacturing support, and administration and organizational development activities for one or multiple facilities through Production, Engineering, Maintenance, Purchasing, Quality, Tooling, and Production Control to ensure efficient production of parts with the best material usage, quality levels, and service that exceed the customer’s expectations. Responsible for ensuring all key measures are met from plant and business operations. Leads and promotes matters related to safety, health, environmental, labor control, equipment, material, processes, and customer relations.
 
ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS
 
A. Serve as management consultant to assigned locations ensuring the management of the company aligns with North American Stamping Group, LLC standard operating procedures and provide subject matter expertise and assistance to increase operating and management efficiency.
 
B. Lead, plan, and manage all manufacturing activities and related functions at assigned locations including production, engineering, maintenance, purchasing, quality, tooling, and production control to ensure safety and quality and to meet and exceed customer and company requirements.
 
1. Lead manufacturing supervision in utilizing Total Quality Production System (TQPS) techniques to standardize processes/methods and to identify manufacturing problems and raw materials/components supply, and eliminate waste.
 
2. Ensure that feasibility studies are carried out correctly for the products to be manufactured at the facility, compatible with the footprint, investment, and quality capabilities planned.
 
3. Develop and monitor Lean activities and a manufacturing continuous improvement system.
 
4. Review launch products and engineering changes implementation and provide direction for successful launch.
 
5. Plan and organize layouts for line changes due to volume changes or manpower reductions.
 
6. Maintain contact with interdepartmental managers to provide feedback when dealing with process or material changes.
 
7. Hold daily staff meetings to communicate daily objectives and discuss successes, failures, and countermeasure activity.
 
8. Ensure NASG philosophies, systems, and processes are being followed at all times.
 
9. Maintain Master Capacity Plan for the facility for accurate budget and capital needs.
 
C. Lead and direct both strategic planning and tactical execution of manufacturing, manufacturing support, and administration functions.
 
D. Understand and execute all plant policies and procedures.
 
1. Structure and implement plant policies and procedures to ensure safe and efficient operation of the company and its associates.
 
2. Ensure alignment of plant policies and procedures, including associate handbook, with corporate policies and procedures.
 
3. Manage plant practices and procedures in compliance with company and industry standards (e.g., IATF16949 and ISO14001).
 
E. Lead development and management of annual plan, budget, key measures, operating efficiency, and cost control.
 
1. Develop annual plan and budget for plant aligned with corporate goals as the foundation to keep the plant moving in a safe, quality conscious, and efficient upward trend.
 
2. Review quotations of new products to ensure compliance with the manufacturing footprint and investment/manpower plans.
 
3. Administer annual plan that incorporates safety, quality, productivity, cost reduction, and associate morale.
 
4. Mutually establish goals and objectives with VP, Manufacturing quarterly.
 
5. Ensure plant goals are met and kept on track.
 
6. Develop, plan, and maintain the budget for plant including making adjustments to achieve targets. Maintain direct and indirect labor budgets while meeting quality and order fill requirements.
 
7. Review and track posted daily, weekly, and monthly goals (including Key Measure targets and results), spot potential problems, and lead in formulating and implementing short-term and long-term countermeasures and solutions.
 
8. Review and plan headcount weekly for labor cost control and operating equipment efficiency (OEE).
 
9. Support and resolve accounts receivable issues with the finance team to ensure timely collection.
 
10. Oversee the monthly reporting documents that are finalized for the plant, ensuring accuracy and completion. Report out monthly reports with targets. Conduct Monthly Management Review meetings.
 
11. Lead management discussions and planning sessions to help formulate cost reduction, waste reduction, product improvement, and problem solving activities, and present operational performance daily/weekly.
 
F. Act as key contact for customers and local industry groups.
 
1. Conduct plant tours and host customer meetings as required.
 
2. Ensure all parts are made to customer requirements in accordance with company policy.
 
3. Support activities to develop and improve customer relations and obtain future business opportunities.
 
4. Develop relationships with local industry groups including those related to manufacturing, automotive, human resources, education and training, legal services, and financial.
 
G. Manage and direct staff in assigned Manufacturing group with a focus on equipment, processes, human resource allocation, cost management, setting priorities, removing roadblocks, and leading through problem identification and resolution, and implementation of short- and long-term corrective actions to manufacturing problems.
 
1. Assign production and engineering staff to support all assigned projects on time and budget with accepted quality.
 
2. Lead staff in activities to meet and improve standard costs of operation both in material and output; minimize downtime; maintain good 5S at all times; reduce cost of quality internal/external failure and PPM; optimize material utilization; optimize raw material, WIP, and finished goods inventory; improve material specifications; and maintain preventative maintenance program.
 
3. Develop and maintain positive associate relations centered on mutual trust, dignity, respect, fairness, consistency, two-way communication, teamwork, and harmony.
 
4. Provide direction and motivation to associates emphasizing quality, efficiency, productivity, cost reduction, safety and health, and morale.
 
5. Ensure further development of associates through performance evaluation, development of training plans, feedback, coaching, and cascade training. Update associate training matrix and schedule any needed training.
 
6. Conduct monthly meetings with associates to communicate state of business.
 
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS/REQUIREMENTS
 
 
**Education:** 

* Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Engineering, or related field preferred, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* Lean Six Sigma certification preferred.
* Auditor training through ISO 14001/IATF16949 preferred.

**Experience:** 

* At least 10 years of functional leadership experience as a manager in a manufacturing environment, preferably automotive stamping.
* Minimum of 12 years of relevant work experience in a manufacturing environment, preferably in automotive stamping, welding, and/or related components (e.g., seating, emissions, ride control, NVH, tooling, and other miscellaneous components).

**Personal/Technical Skills:** 

* General understanding and working knowledge of manufacturing, assembly, and welding equipment and tooling including design, automation, robotics, or manufacturing processes (and all secondary related processes) relating to automotive stamping.
* Working knowledge of tool, gauges and equipment design, automation, robotics, and/or manufacturing processes.
* Practical experience and working knowledge of Basic Equipment Care (BEC) and Preventive Maintenance Optimization (PMO) systems for machinery, tooling, and gauges.
* Practical experience applying Lean principles in an automotive environment.
* General understanding and practical work experience with automotive quality systems and processes.
* Working knowledge of material types specifications and characteristics used in automotive stampings.
* Practical experience applying Total Quality Production System (TQPS) principles in an automotive environment.
* Thorough understanding of company product, trade terminology, quality management and control systems and techniques, manufacturing processes including material controls, work flow, scheduling, kanban, and equipment and machine operation.
* Versed in statistical data entry and utilization of trend analysis.
* Ability to implement plans to control and maintain safety, quality, 5S, cost, and efficiency for assigned areas.
* Strong organization, time management, and planning skills and ability to manage multiple tasks with tight deadlines.
* Ability to teach managers, group leaders, team leaders, and associates in basic fundamental skills and facilitate Job Instruction Training (JIT).
* Must have the ability to monitor and adjust operating plans and budgets as needed to achieve operational goals, cost reduction objectives, and/or profitability targets.
* Will possess the organizational skills necessary to maintain company records in compliance with the Manufacturing Department and TS16949/ISO 14001 procedures.
* Must be able to work a fixed or rotating shift schedule, including daily or weekend overtime, and have the ability to work a schedule that allows completion of the job on a daily basis.

**Language Skills:** 

* Must be able to speak, read, write, and understand the primary language (English) used in the workplace.

**Computer/Software:** 

* Solid working knowledge and experience with Microsoft Office and other computer-based applications (e.g., MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint, MS Outlook, Internet, etc.).
* Working knowledge and experience with ERP/MRP software.

**Travel:** 
Must be willing to travel up to 30% to visit customers, suppliers, and other manufacturing sites.
 
 
North American Stamping Group is a drug-free and smoke-free workplace.

existing_roles.description:
**Lassonde Pappas & Co.** is a US Leader in beverage manufacturing dedicated to our team members, customers and consumers satisfaction. We remain committed to our small-town roots and rural values. **Hardworking** and **caring** are qualities that make our teams special. Since 1942, we’ve been producing delicious products for our customers across the country!

To provide the best for our customers, we focus on building the best team by creating and advancing an inclusive environment amongst our diverse workforces. If you’re passionate about customer satisfaction, reliable, and committed to being and doing better, join us!

**We value each of our employees’ total wellbeing. To support employees in all stages of their wellness journey, we have a robust benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage options, growth and development potential, along with 401-K, Life & Disability Insurance, PTO, Tuition Reimbursement, Health Fairs, Gym Membership Discounts, and so much more!**

*Pay Range for this position is: $155,000-$200,000 plus annual bonus, depending on experience and geographical location.*

**POSITION SUMMARY** 
The Environmental Health and Safety Director leads the development, implementation, and performance of health, safety, and environmental programs and policies at Lassonde Pappas & Co. Inc. facilities, to maintain compliance with applicable national and local regulations and to ensure a safe, healthy working environment for all employees. This role reports to the VP of Manufacturing for the US and is based out of our Cherry Hill, New Jersey location.

**Primary Responsibilities include*****:***

* Oversee and ensure the organization’s compliance with local, state, and federal environment, health, and safety regulations including (but not limited to) fire safety and OSHA regulations, and keep up with any changes to laws and regulations that impact the organization
* Work closely with the organization’s legal department to ensure that the company is in compliance with these regulations
* Direct audits and work with each plant and its departments to ensure that all company guidelines are being followed
* Manage the safety budget at the manufacturing sites to ensure that appropriate personal protective and safety equipment is available as needed to prevent injuries and provide for a safe and healthy work environment
* Develop, implement, and evaluate programs, policies, and procedures related to health, safety, and environmental issues in the workplace, and ensure that environmental policy and procedure manuals are available and updated at all times to reduce the risk of injury or illness in the workplace
* Prepare, schedule, and execute training to cover emergency procedures, workplace safety, and other relevant topics
* Lead the planning, execution, monitoring and continuous improvement of environmental health and safety programs
* Conduct risk assessments of work sites to identify potential hazards and formulate plans to mitigate them
* Coordinate with insurance carriers to ensure that appropriate coverage is in place to cover any potential risks
* Review the employee accident reports and medical claims to evaluate the need for potential changes to current policies or procedures
* Consult with engineers to ensure that building designs are safe and compliant with current regulations
* Performs other related duties as required and assigned

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Maintain staff by training employees; maintaining a safe, secure, and legal work environment; developing personal growth opportunities.
* Set objectives, monitor performance, and develop individual training plans to support professional development

* Communicate job expectations; planning, monitoring, and assessing job results; coaching, and counseling employees; developing, coordinating, and enforcing systems, procedures, and productivity standards.
* Establish strategic goals; identifying and evaluating trends; choosing a course of action; defining objectives; evaluating outcomes.
* Set strategic direction and coordinate the work of others to achieve objectives.

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE**

**Minimum Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Safety, Occupational Safety and Health, or related field required; Masters degree desirable.

* Minimum 8 years working experience in Supply Chain environment in Food and Beverage or other perishable goods
* 5+ years of safety and environmental experience in a manufacturing environment. Experience with a union manufacturing environment is a plus.
* Excellent negotiation skills and the ability to influence others while maintaining professionalism
* Proficient in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook (knowledge in Excel should extend past spreadsheet manipulation and should include creation of formulas)
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills
* Detailed oriented and can multi-task
* Excellent time management skills

**Additional Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in the food/beverage industry
* Experience in Manufacturing or production environment
* Experience with risk management and project management
* Must pay high attention to detail and have strong interpersonal, communication, and observation skills
* Experience in report writing
* Proven organizational skills
* Ability to direct, coach, and train others
* Consultative, influential, strategic thinking and problem-solving skills

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS & WORKING CONDITIONS**

This position requires sufficient physical ability to work in a typical office setting; driving a motor vehicle and occasionally working in the field/production setting.

**FREQUENT:** sitting, upward and downward flexion of neck; fine finger dexterity and light to moderate finger pressure to include extended periods of keyboard and mouse use, side-to-side turning of neck, walking, standing, bending and stooping, pushing/pulling, twisting at waist, moderate wrist torque to twist equipment knobs and dials.

**OCCASIONAL:** squatting, kneeling, reach above and at shoulder height, moderate grasp to manipulate reference books and manuals; lifting objects weighing 20 – 35 lbs. from below waist to above shoulders and transporting distances up to 50 feet.

**VISION:** Ability to see in the normal visual range with or without correction.

**HEARING:** Ability to hear in the normal audio range with or without correction.

**Overview**

We are seeking an experienced, results-driven **Plant Manager** to lead all daily manufacturing and facility operations. In this role, you will oversee production performance, quality standards, equipment maintenance, and environmental health and safety (EHS/OSHA) compliance. You will manage plant-level budgets, drive improvement initiatives, and build a high-performing, accountable team.

**Responsibilities**

* Provide leadership, coordination, direction and oversight of management/supervisory personnel assigned to power generation facilities.
* Review, analyze, plan, coordinate, and lead all activities within the Operations Department.
* Ensure plant availability and execution of operating and maintenance schedules in conjunction with Plant Staff. • Enforce OSHA, NERC and Environmental permit regulations, investigating accidents, and tracking safety violations.
* Improve processes to optimize asset performance.
* Direct preventive/predictive maintenance programs and coordinate major plant overhauls or planned outages to minimize downtown.
* Establish goals to provide continual improvement in operational productivity and quality.
* Facilitate operational and process engineering changes as necessary.
* Provide oversight to foster an environment that encourages employee involvement.
* Provide guidance and support to ensure safety, environmental, and regulatory compliance.
* Coordinate fulfillment of obligations to its contract counterparties and the energy markets.
* Prepare and manage annual operating and labor budgets, vendor contracts, parts inventory and cost control initiatives.
* Hire, train, schedule and evaluate plant operators, engineers and maintenance staff.
* Ensure compliance with all company standards, practices and policies.
* Oversee the administration of all computerized databases, file systems, and reporting systems for the collection and processing of plant related data.
* Perform other duties as deemed necessary by Owner and VP of Operations.

**Skills**

* A bachelor's degree in business or engineering discipline or equivalent experience preferred.
* A minimum of 10-15 years’ experience in hydroelectric, steam and/or electric power plant operations.
* A minimum of 5 years’ management experience.
* Practical knowledge of power generation systems, boilers, gas turbines, and equipment maintenance.
* Mechanical knowledge, electrical systems familiarity, and engineering troubleshooting ability; technical proficiency with plant equipment and P&IDs.
* Understanding of water and wastewater treatment, pipelines, oil and gas operations, safety regulations, and environmental compliance.

existing_roles.title: Director of Contract Manufacturing
existing_roles.description:
**Position Summary:**

**The Director of Contract Manufacturing** focuses activities and resources in the organization around value creation and has responsibility for the success of the value stream. Unlike Steffes’ product-line business units, Contract Manufacturing does not own a product line; it markets and sells Steffes’ engineering and manufacturing services, building to customer designs, specifications, and requirements.

The Director of Contract Manufacturing understands key system constraints, quickly identifies critical process issues and successfully maintains key customer relationships. Has management responsibility for the strategy, relationship management, pricing and margin.

This role must have excellent business, manufacturing, and technical knowledge; as well as interpersonal skills to communicate and be an influencer, both internal and external to the organization.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Maintains responsibility for assigned business unit, including profitability, business development and budgeting.

* Develops sales and promotional strategies for Steffes’ engineering and manufacturing services within the Value Stream.

* Sets vision, defines direction, influences and inspires others, aligns and leads teams to create value and grow the business.

* Responsible for increasing and tracking contract manufacturing revenue and market share.

* Responsible for advancing key customer relationships.

* Works with other department leaders to aid in allocation of resources and capacity to achieve specific business results.

* Coaches and assists team members.

* Sets clear expectations for the customer program life cycle, from quote through production and delivery, and ensures the team understands goals and expectations.

* Identifies risks and establishes suitable actions.

* Responsible for overall customer experience and customer care.

* Maintains a deep understanding of Steffes’ engineering and production processes, capabilities, and capacity.

* Ensures accurate and timely technical reviews of customer designs, drawings, and requirements.

* Establishes pricing based on cost estimates and market value such that market share and profitability goals can be met.

* Maintains a good understanding of competing contract manufacturers and engineering service providers, including their capabilities, marketing strategies, and relative costs. Be capable of effectively communicating this information with the sales department and other functional areas.

* Works with account managers to develop strategies to sell Steffes’ engineering and manufacturing services to current and prospective customers.

* Ensures Steffes’ contract manufacturing services are competitive from the standpoint of quality, reliability, cost, lead time, and on-time shipping by calling out deficiencies and seeing proper action is initiated to correct problem areas.

* Monthly maintains financial forecasting and price reviews.

* Communicates with internal staff on a regular basis to understand their business problems and help find solutions.

* Maintains a positive work atmosphere by acting and communicating in a collaborative manner with customers, suppliers, co-workers, and management.

* Helps company meet its Strategic, Quality, and Safety objectives.

* Assists with development and execution of annual sales plans.

* Establishes and maintains guidelines for pursuing and accepting new business.

* Daily monitors shipping activity, costing and pricing to ensure sales and profitability goals are being achieved.

* Assists CFO with review of Terms & Conditions and MSA’s and negotiates with the customer to resolve differences.

* Ensures prompt and satisfactory resolution to external quality issues on customer parts and assemblies.

* Other duties may be assigned

**Job Requirements/Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Engineering or equivalent experience preferred.
* 5 years of experience working in engineering, manufacturing, marketing, or sales
* Experience selling or managing engineering and/or contract manufacturing services with customers.
* Intermediate computer knowledge (Windows, email, internet, etc.)
* Written and verbal communication skills
* Overnight travel is required occasionally

-OR-

* An acceptable combination of education and experience

**Functional & Cognitive Requirements of Position**

* This position requires walking, sitting or standing to a significant degree.
* Must have the ability to lift 50 pounds from floor to waist, carry 50 pounds, and push and/or pull up to 50 pounds.
* Must have the ability to climb ladders and/or stairs.
* Stooping, crouching, kneeling and bending.
* Handling, feeling, and gripping would be required for some activities.
* Visual acuity is required to inspect work completed.
* This role may be subject to internal and external environmental conditions.
* Learn new tasks, remember processes, maintain focus, complete tasks independently, make timely decisions in the context of a workflow, ability to communicate with visitors, ability to complete tasks in situations that have a speed or productivity quota.

**Core Values:** 
**Trust:** We promote growth and long-term success by making wise decisions with trust as an essential component. 
**Respect:** We unleash creative talents of our diverse workforce by treating each other the way we would like to be treated. 
**Teamwork**: We believe people achieve much more by working together. 
**Integrity:** We follow through and keep our word while being open, honest, ethical, and fair. 
**Safety:** We view our co-workers as family members of our business and strive to ensure safety for all. • Humility: We recognize and appreciate strengths and contributions beyond one’s self. We are modest, genuine, and authentic. 
 
**Core Expectations:** 
**Customer Service** - Demonstrate excellent customer service and display a positive attitude and behavior consistent with the Steffes Code of Conduct and Core Values. 
**Environmental, Health, Safety (EHS)** – Perform work in compliance with EHS training and identified procedures/standard work. Report any EHS incident or concern to your supervisor immediately. Cooperate and contribute to the overall success of the EHS program. 
**Quality** – Participate in job-specific training. Complete work as indicated by standard work, processes, and/or procedures. If your work can’t be completed as required, notify your supervisor immediately for guidance. 
**Conduct** - Demonstrate and support the Steffes Code of Conduct. 
**Policies and Procedures** - Demonstrate and support Steffes Policies and Procedures by: 
o Using tact, sound judgement, and maintaining a professional attitude in communication and relationships with others. 
o Striving to deliver the best quality in daily work. 
o Promoting a positive image of Steffes and its products. 
o Being timely and punctual in attendance and following all policies and procedures.

*Equal Opportunity Employer*
