existing_roles.title: Director of Quality
existing_roles.description:
**Director of Quality**

**Location**

Carmel, IN • Memphis, TN • St. Louis, MO • Malden, MO • Peoria, IL • Other Illinois locations

**Leadership**

Directly manages at least two quality team members

**Travel**

Regular travel to manufacturing facilities and business locations, as needed

Weaver Popcorn is seeking a seasoned quality leader ready to step into a broader Director-level role. The Director of Quality provides strategic and operational leadership for food safety, quality assurance, regulatory compliance, audit readiness, and continuous improvement across the organization’s food manufacturing operations. This leader will strengthen and standardize quality systems, develop quality talent, and partner with plant and business leaders to ensure products consistently meet company, customer, certification, and regulatory requirements.

This is a hands-on leadership role for an experienced food manufacturing quality professional who can set direction while remaining actively engaged with plant teams, audits, investigations, corrective actions, and day-to-day execution.

**HOW WILL YOU HELP US GROW?**
==============================

**Quality & Food Safety Leadership**
------------------------------------

* Develop and lead the company’s quality and food safety strategy, priorities, policies, procedures, and performance expectations across manufacturing locations.
* Ensure quality assurance and food safety programs are effectively implemented, maintained, verified, and continuously improved.
* Establish and oversee grain and popcorn quality standards from grower receipt and bulk storage through processing, bagging, and shipment, ensuring consistent quality controls throughout the supply chain.
* Provide visible leadership on the manufacturing floor through routine plant engagement, risk reviews, verification activities, and follow-up on quality concerns.
* Build a culture of accountability, prevention, compliance, and continuous improvement across Quality, Operations, Supply Chain, Sales, and other partner functions.

**SQF, Audits & Regulatory Compliance**
---------------------------------------

* Lead and maintain SQF certification programs, including system ownership, audit preparation, certification readiness, corrective actions, and ongoing compliance.
* Plan, lead, and oversee internal, customer, certification, and regulatory audits of food manufacturing facilities.
* Ensure timely closure of audit findings, nonconformances, corrective and preventive actions, and related verification activities.
* Lead cross-functional Food Safety/HACCP, risk assessment, prerequisite program, and food quality teams.
* Monitor applicable food safety and quality requirements and translate them into practical operating standards and controls.
* Ensure effective quality controls for bulk grain storage, bin holds and releases, sampling, testing, and corn disposition prior to processing, including compliance with applicable phytosanitary requirements.

**Quality Management Systems**
------------------------------

* Own the effective use and continuous improvement of quality management system software, including document control, audits, corrective actions, training records, verification, and reporting.
* Standardize quality documentation, specifications, procedures, policies, records, and reporting across facilities.
* Use quality data, trend analysis, and leading and lagging indicators to identify risk, establish priorities, and improve performance.
* Ensure effective controls for ingredient sampling, product verification, environmental monitoring, sanitation verification, traceability, and other core quality programs.
* Provide oversight of corn testing and laboratory quality programs, including mycotoxin testing, internal and third-party sample testing, review of test results, and appropriate product disposition based on quality and food safety requirements.

**People Leadership & Cross-Functional Partnership**
----------------------------------------------------

* Lead, coach, and develop a quality team of at least two direct reports, with potential for broader team responsibility as the function grows.
* Set clear goals, define accountabilities, assess performance, strengthen technical capability, and create development plans for quality team members.
* Partner with Plant Managers and Operations leaders to resolve quality issues without compromising food safety, customer requirements, or regulatory compliance.
* Establish and enforce hold/release and product disposition standards, with authority to stop processing or bagging operations and place grain, ingredients, or finished product on hold when food safety or quality requirements are not met.
* Partner with Sales and Customer Service to respond to customer documentation requests, audits, samples, complaints, and quality-related inquiries.
* Lead investigations into customer complaints, product or process deviations, and recurring issues; ensure root cause analysis and sustainable corrective action.
* Oversee nonconforming material, product holds, rework, release, and disposition processes, partnering with Operations and suppliers to ensure timely resolution and prevent recurrence.
* Provide clear quality updates, risk assessments, recommendations, and performance reporting to senior leadership and other decision-makers.

**WHAT DO YOU NEED TO HAVE?**
=============================

* Bachelor's degree in food science, Food Safety, Microbiology, Chemistry, Biology, Engineering, or related fields.
* 8–10+ years of progressive quality or food safety experience in the food manufacturing industry.
* At least 5 years of people-management experience, including progressive supervisory and manager-level responsibility.
* Proven leadership of SQF certification programs and successful food manufacturing audits.
* Demonstrated knowledge of food safety principles, quality assurance procedures and policies, HACCP-based programs, risk assessment, corrective action, and preventive controls.
* Experience leading internal, customer, certification, and/or regulatory audits across food manufacturing environments.
* Hands-on experience with quality management system software and electronic quality records.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through influence, develop teams, manage competing priorities, and drive consistent execution across locations.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate quality risk and technical requirements to operational and executive audiences.
* Ability to travel regularly to manufacturing facilities and business locations, as needed.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Experience in grain, corn, popcorn, milling, ingredient, or related agricultural processing.
* SQF Practitioner experience and formal training in HACCP, PCQI, internal auditing, root cause analysis, or preventive controls.
* Experience supporting multiple manufacturing sites or standardizing quality systems across locations.
* Experience with supplier quality, customer complaint management, environmental monitoring, traceability, recall readiness, and food defense programs.

**WHAT DOES SUCCESS LOOK LIKE?**
================================

* Consistent audit and certification readiness across facilities.
* Stronger standardization and adoption of quality systems, procedures, and records.
* Timely, well-documented corrective action with verified effectiveness.
* Reduced recurrence of quality issues and customer complaints through disciplined root cause analysis.
* A capable, accountable quality team with clear goals and development plans.
* Credible, practical partnership with Operations and business leaders while maintaining independent quality judgment.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT & SCHEDULE**
===============================

This role operates across office and food manufacturing environments and requires regular presence in production areas. The typical schedule is Monday through Friday; however, the Director of Quality must be available outside normal business hours, including occasional evenings or weekends, when operational, audit, customer, or food safety needs require support. Regular travel is expected based on business needs.

**HOW WILL WE HELP YOU GROW?**
==============================

* Competitive compensation.
* Three weeks of paid time off in the first year.
* 401(k) plan with a company match of 100% of employee deferrals up to 10%.
* Health, vision, dental, life, and disability insurance beginning the first day of the month following 30 days of employment.
* Education reimbursement of up to $15,000 per year.

**EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY**
================================

Weaver Popcorn is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and associates. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without regard to any status protected by applicable law.

*The role responsibilities are many, various, and not limited to those written in this document*

As leaders in infection prevention, they currently own and operate the most HLAC-accredited facilities in the industry. With one of the highest customer retention rates in the industry – 97% – ImageFIRST is dedicated to improving patient satisfaction and making staff happy with our white glove service!

Check out our company page: https://www.imagefirst.com/company/

**Director, Operational Excellence - CAPEX**
============================================

**Location:** East Coast (Northeast Preferred) 
**Travel:** Approximately 50%

**Position Summary**
--------------------

ImageFIRST is seeking a strategic, hands-on **Director, Operational Excellence** to lead enterprise-wide engineering initiatives, capital project planning, and operational improvement efforts across our national network of healthcare laundry facilities.

This newly created leadership role will serve as a key partner to Operations and the Senior Leadership Team, driving long-term asset strategy, **capital investment planning**, engineering support, and operational sustainability. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable developing strategic initiatives, leading complex projects, and rolling up their sleeves to solve operational challenges in the field.

This role offers a unique opportunity to build foundational processes that will standardize engineering practices and strengthen operational performance across the organization.

**Key Responsibilities**

### **Capital Planning & Strategic Investments**

* Identify, prioritize, and develop capital expenditure (Capex) opportunities across the network.
* Build financial justifications, ROI analyses, and business cases for capital investments.
* Present capital recommendations and project proposals to the Senior Leadership Team.
* Partner with Finance and Operations to align capital investments with business strategy and growth objectives.

### **Project Engineering Leadership**

* Lead enterprise engineering projects from concept through implementation.
* Provide technical leadership for facility upgrades, equipment installations, automation initiatives, and operational improvements.
* Ensure projects are completed safely, on schedule, within budget, and with measurable business impact.

### **Engineering Support for Plant Operations**

* Serve as a technical resource for manufacturing and plant leadership across the ImageFIRST network.
* Provide engineering guidance and problem-solving support for facilities requiring operational or technical assistance.

* Lead cross-functional operational improvement initiatives that support network stabilization, sustainability, and long-term operational performance.

### **Safety Leadership**

* Champion a culture of safety across engineering and operational initiatives.
* Ensure engineering projects and equipment installations meet all applicable safety standards and regulatory requirements.

**Qualifications**

* Proven experience managing capital projects and developing ROI-driven business cases.
* Strong knowledge of asset management, equipment lifecycle planning, and reliability.
* Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence stakeholders at all organizational levels.
* Strong financial acumen with experience presenting recommendations to executive leadership.

* Experience supporting multiple manufacturing or industrial facilities.
* Plant management or operations leadership experience.
* Lean Manufacturing, TPM, Six Sigma, or Continuous Improvement experience.
* Military leadership experience is highly valued, particularly candidates who have transitioned into manufacturing, engineering, or operations leadership roles.
* Experience within healthcare services, industrial laundry, textiles, food manufacturing, consumer products, or other asset-intensive industries.

* Results-oriented and highly accountable

* Strong analytical and financial decision-making capabilities
* Collaborative leadership style with the ability to influence across functions

existing_roles.description:
*Aerospace is at a turning point — costs are rising, supply chains are strained, and old ways of building can't keep up. At Neon Aero, we're breaking that mold. We move fast, think big, and combine start-up agility with aerospace expertise to design, build, and scale aircraft in ways the industry has never seen. Our team leverages automation, AI-driven tools, and a fully connected digital backbone to accelerate innovation and reduce barriers to production.*

*Here, you won't just take a job — you'll help reinvent how the world flies. If you're ready to solve complex problems, push technology further, and work alongside some of the brightest minds in aerospace, this is your chance to make a real impact.*

Neon is looking for an Aerospace Quality Director to help build the quality systems, team, and operating discipline needed to take parts and assemblies from prototype into production. This role will lead the quality function across development, manufacturing, supplier quality, and production readiness, ensuring the company can scale with strong process control, repeatability, and compliance. You will play a key role in helping a growing aerospace organization move from fast iteration to reliable production without losing technical rigor.

### **Why This Role Matters**

* Help shape how a growing company scales from prototype builds to stable production.
* Build the quality foundation needed for repeatable manufacturing, stronger yields, and fewer escapes.
* Partner directly with engineering and manufacturing to improve design transfer, process readiness, and production execution.
* Lead the systems and team that drive inspection discipline, nonconformance control, corrective action, and supplier quality.
* Influence how production processes are defined, controlled, and improved as volume and complexity grow.
* Operate in a fast-paced environment where quality decisions directly affect hardware readiness, customer confidence, and operational scale.
* Work across office, lab, and production settings with direct visibility into how quality impacts the business.

### **What You'll Bring**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, quality, manufacturing, aerospace, or a related technical field; equivalent professional experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
* Experience managing a growing department of direct reports responsible for all aspects of product and process quality.
* Significant progressive experience in aerospace quality, manufacturing quality, supplier quality, or quality systems leadership.
* Experience helping move parts, assemblies, or hardware programs from prototype into production.
* Experience building or improving quality systems in a growing manufacturing organization.
* Strong background in inspection planning, process controls, nonconformance management, and corrective action.
* Experience working cross-functionally with engineering, manufacturing, and supply chain teams to improve quality and production readiness.
* Experience with supplier quality management and supplier issue resolution.
* Strong problem-solving skills, judgment, communication, and ability to drive accountability across teams.
* Ability to work across office, lab, and production environments.
* Ability to support periods of increased workload tied to builds, ramp activity, and issue resolution.
* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States.
* May be required to meet export control, ITAR, confidentiality, or site access requirements.

#### **Preferred**

* Advanced degree in a relevant technical discipline; equivalent professional experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
* ASQ certification or equivalent quality credential.
* Experience with first article inspection, process validation, control plans, or production quality planning tools.
* Experience in high-growth aerospace, defense, or advanced hardware manufacturing environments.
* Experience building quality organizations during production scale-up.

### **Why Join Us**

* Work alongside elite engineering talent and innovators from across aerospace and tech.
* Be part of a team moving faster than the industry standard.
* Shape solutions that are lower-cost, autonomous, and scalable — the future of aviation.
* Competitive compensation, including equity participation, growth opportunities, and full health benefits (health, vision, dental, 401(k)) designed to support you in and out of work.

*Neon Aero, Inc is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected status under applicable law.*

*We believe that diverse perspectives drive innovation, and we welcome candidates from all backgrounds to apply.*

*All final candidates must successfully complete a background check and drug screening as a condition of employment.*

**At this time, Neon Aero and its divisions are not accepting unsolicited resumes from third-party recruiters or staffing agencies.**

existing_roles.title: Plant/Manufacturing Director
existing_roles.description:
Job Summary
 
Maker’s Pride is seeking a proven, enterprise-minded Plant Director to lead our largest manufacturing facility in McComb, Ohio, a site of more than 1,600 Team Members that is critical to the success of our business. The Plant Director holds full accountability for the safety, quality, service, cost, and people performance of a large-scale co-manufacturing operation, and serves as the senior leader on site and the face of the plant to customers, Team Members, and the community.
 
This role requires a seasoned operations executive who has led large, complex plants of 1,000+ Team Members, can build and develop a strong leadership bench, and can balance day-to-day execution with long-term strategy. The Plant Director partners closely with senior leadership and corporate functions to deliver the plant’s operating plan, drive operational excellence, and position McComb for sustained growth.
 
 
Key Responsibilities
 

* Operational Leadership: Lead all plant operations, including production, packaging, maintenance, engineering, quality, warehouse, and supply chain, to consistently deliver safety, quality, service, and cost targets across multiple shifts and lines.
* P&L and Financial Accountability: Own the plant’s operating plan, budget, and financial performance, including labor, overtime, yield, waste, and capital spend. Identify and execute cost-reduction and margin-improvement opportunities.
* Strategic Planning: Develop and execute a multi-year plant strategy aligned to enterprise goals, covering capacity, capital investment, automation, new business onboarding, and talent.
* Production Planning and Capacity: Partner with Supply Chain, Planning, and Customer teams to build production schedules and resource plans that optimize throughput, labor utilization, and on-time, in-full performance.
* Quality and Food Safety: Ensure strict adherence to quality, food safety, and regulatory requirements (e.g., FDA, GMP, HACCP, and customer and third-party audit standards). Drive corrective and preventive actions and maintain audit readiness at all times.
* Safety Culture: Champion a zero-harm culture. Enforce safety policies, lead regular audits and incident reviews, and hold the leadership team accountable for proactive hazard prevention and compliance.
* Workforce Strategy and Labor Relations: Partner with HR to attract, retain, and engage a large and diverse workforce. Drive staffing stability, reduce turnover, manage overtime effectively, and foster positive Team Member and labor relations, including compliance with applicable employment and labor laws and agreements.
* Customer and Partner Relationships: Serve as the senior site representative with co-manufacturing customers, hosting visits and audits, resolving escalations, and building long-term trust. Collaborate with suppliers to ensure timely delivery of materials and finished goods.
* Continuous Improvement: Lead a data-driven operational excellence program using Lean, Six Sigma, or similar methodologies to eliminate waste, improve OEE and yield, and standardize best practices across shifts.
* Capital and Asset Management: Oversee capital planning, project execution, and asset reliability to ensure equipment, infrastructure, and facilities support safe, efficient, and scalable operations.
* Reporting and Executive Communication: Provide regular, transparent reporting on safety, quality, production, financial, and workforce KPIs to senior leadership, with clear analysis, risks, and recommendations.
* Community and Site Presence: Represent Maker’s Pride in the McComb community and maintain a visible, accessible leadership presence on the plant floor across all shifts.

Supervisory Responsibilities
 

* Leadership of a Large Organization: Provide direct leadership to the plant leadership team and overall leadership of 1,600+ Team Members, including managers, supervisors, technicians, and support staff.
* Talent Development: Build a strong leadership bench through coaching, performance management, succession planning, and development of high-potential leaders.
* Culture and Accountability: Foster a culture of safety, quality, teamwork, accountability, respect, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications
 

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field required; Master’s degree or MBA preferred.
* Experience: 15+ years of progressive manufacturing operations experience, including 7+ years in a senior plant leadership role (Plant Manager, Plant Director, or equivalent).
* Scale: Demonstrated success leading large, complex, multi-shift plants of 1,000+ Team Members, with full P&L accountability.
* Industry: Experience in co-manufacturing, food, beverage, or other high-volume, regulated manufacturing environments strongly preferred.
* Operational Excellence: Track record of delivering measurable improvements in safety, quality, productivity, and cost. Lean, Six Sigma, or similar certification desirable.
* Workforce Leadership: Proven ability to lead, motivate, and develop a large, diverse workforce, including strong experience with staffing, retention, and employee and labor relations. Experience in a unionized environment is a plus.
* Regulatory Knowledge: Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, food safety and quality standards, and regulatory requirements.
* Technology: Proficiency in ERP systems and Microsoft Office Suite; experience with manufacturing software (e.g., SAP, Oracle) is a plus.
* Leadership Skills: Strategic thinker with excellent executive presence, communication, and decision-making skills; able to influence at all levels of the organization and with customers.
* Analytical Skills: Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities with a focus on data-driven decision-making.

The information provided in this document provides an overview of the most common duties, qualifications, and demands of the position. It is not intended to be a comprehensive summary of the role, and the duties, qualifications, and demands of the position are subject to change without notice. The expectations provided here may also be modified if an employee with a disability could effectively meet the expectations for the role with reasonable accommodation.

existing_roles.description:
Reporting to the SVP and CFO for Manufacturing, Supply Chain and Quality, the Director, Site Manufacturing Controller serves as the senior finance leader and strategic business partner for the Salt Lake City manufacturing site. This role provides enterprise-level financial leadership across site operations, translating manufacturing performance, capacity, productivity, quality, inventory, and capital investment drivers into clear business insights and actions. The Director advises site and functional leadership, challenges operating and investment assumptions, leads long-range financial planning, and drives sustainable improvement in manufacturing cost, working capital, and capital efficiency. The role is accountable for the integrity of site financial results, product costing, forecasting, internal controls, and decision support in alignment with company policies and applicable accounting standards. The Director leads and develops the local manufacturing controlling team and connects the Salt Lake City site with regional, global, and corporate finance stakeholders.

**Primary Duties**
------------------

* **Strategic finance leadership and business partnership:** Act as the senior finance advisor to Salt Lake City site leadership and a key member of the site leadership team. Shape site strategy, operating priorities, and resource allocation by translating business and manufacturing drivers into financial implications, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
* **Site performance and value creation:** Own the financial performance framework for the site, including profit and loss, cost of goods, manufacturing variances, productivity, yield, scrap, labor and overhead, fixed-cost absorption, inventory, and working capital. Establish performance routines, identify root causes, and hold leaders accountable for corrective actions and measurable value delivery.
* **Long-range planning, budgeting, and forecasting:** Lead the site financial planning cycle, including strategic plans, annual budgets, rolling forecasts, scenario modeling, and sensitivity analysis. Ensure plans reflect realistic assumptions for volume, mix, capacity, headcount, compensation, inflation, productivity, and supply constraints.
* **Capital investment and portfolio governance:** Provide financial leadership for major capital investments, capacity expansion, automation, digitalization, facility improvements, and cost-reduction programs. Set standards for business cases, challenge assumptions, recommend priorities, assess risk and return, and oversee post-investment benefit tracking.
* **Product costing and inventory governance:** Direct site product costing, standard cost development, inventory valuation, cycle counts, physical inventory, excess and obsolete inventory analysis, and cost improvement tracking. Partner with global finance and operations to strengthen costing accuracy and harmonize practices across the manufacturing network.
* **Financial close, reporting, and executive communication:** Oversee accurate and timely month-end and year-end close activities for the site. Deliver concise, decision-oriented reporting and executive commentary that explains results, outlook, key risks, opportunities, and required actions to site, regional, and global leaders.
* **Controls, compliance, and audit readiness:** Maintain a strong internal control environment and ensure compliance with company financial policies, applicable accounting requirements, and audit standards. Lead remediation of internal and external audit findings, strengthen financial governance, and proactively address control or compliance risks.
* **Cross-functional and global influence:** Partner with Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Engineering, Procurement, Human Resources, Information Systems, and Corporate Finance. Represent the Salt Lake City site in regional and global finance forums and influence standards, priorities, and decisions beyond the local organization.
* **Transformation and continuous improvement:** Sponsor and lead improvements in financial processes, management reporting, data quality, analytics, systems, and operating rhythms. Use lean thinking, automation, and standardized tools to improve speed, insight, control, and efficiency.
* **Organization leadership and talent development:** Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing site controlling team. Set clear expectations, build succession and capability plans, allocate resources, and create an inclusive culture of accountability, collaboration, sound judgment, and continuous improvement.

existing_roles.description:
**Department:** Operations **Job Status:** Full Time

**FLSA Status:** Exempt **Reports To:** President

**Job Type:** Non-Union **Amount of Travel Required:** Occasional

**Work Schedule:** Monday – Friday

Evenings, weekends, Holidays as needed. **Positions Supervised:** Production Staff

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Director of Manufacturing executes the company operating plan within capital and operating budget parameters. The Director of Manufacturing works with the executive leadership team to develop strategies and objectives to maximize productivity and profitability. Analyzes production trends, forecasts future requirements, solve problems, motivates & develops employees.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**

**Essential Functions Statement(s)**

 

* Improve operational efficiencies to reduce total production costs while meeting specific product volume needs
* Check and verify production records, handle questions or concerns of inventory shortages or overages and address problems with inventory control.
* Coordinate production schedules to meet sales demand. Adjust production as necessary to meet seasonal demands ahead of schedule.
* Ensure consistency in collective bargaining agreement and provide support during contract negotiations
* Effect necessary communication and motivation to staff. Monitors individual performance via observation and review of various productivity measures. Counsels and disciplines as necessary.
* Provides production required safety leadership and training and is responsible for improved safety performance
* Oversees all production planning and executing against demand signals.
* Oversees facility maintenance team, including Cap-Ex planning and execution.
* Provides input on new product development.
* Ensure compliance with all appropriate health and food safety regulations and cleanliness, including audit preparation
* Manage customer complaint process.
* OSHA, Federal and State requirements are followed with the facility and equipment.
* Attends the Executive, Senior Management, and Safety Committee Meetings
* Maintain work area in a neat, orderly and sanitary manner.
* Correctly and promptly follow specified company procedures required for the appropriate handling of all.
* Emergency Responses and Safety practices.

**POSITION QUALIFICATIONS**

**Competency Statement(s)**

* Communication, Written – Ability to communicate in writing clearly and concisely.
* Collaboration - Collaborates positively to effectively build relationships with customers and co-workers to achieve company objectives and contribute to overall organizational success. Works effectively within a diverse environment. Exhibits a positive attitude and contributes to overall team success.
* Organized – Being organized or following a systematic method of performing a task.
* Communication, Oral – Ability to communicate effectively with others using the spoken word.
* Responsible – Ability to be held accountable or answerable for one’s conduct.
* Honesty / Integrity – Ability to be truthful and be seen as credible in the workplace.
* Accountability – Ability to accept responsibility and account for his/her actions.
* Reliability – The trait of being dependable and trustworthy.
* Friendly – Ability to exhibit a cheerful demeanor toward others.
* Customer Oriented – Ability to take care of the customer’s needs while following company procedures.

**Mental Demands:**

* Ability to work under stressful conditions
* Able to interact with others with courtesy and tact
* Ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects in an organized and efficient manner
* Ability to respond to crisis situations in a calm and effective manner
* Ability to complete projects on schedule

**Communication Demands:**

The position requires talking to co-workers, customers, vendors; requires written communications to and from co-workers, customers and vendors, talking on the telephone; requires responding to written or verbal requests of co-workers, customers and vendors; requires training/giving verbal and written instructions; requires receiving verbal and written instructions; requires writing/composing written language; requires reading; requires visiting/working at other work-sites; Ability to communicate via the latest technologies required for the position.

**Reasonable Accommodations Statement**

Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) safety rules and HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points) required; strong interpersonal skills with an understanding of diverse backgrounds and an emphasis on communication: training, team building, negotiation skills, interdepartmental interaction, leadership and supervision (motivation, directing) and management (planning, budgeting, projecting revenues, analyzing trends); union labor relations, compliance with federal and state regulations,

existing_roles.title: Director of Program Management, Manufacturing
existing_roles.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

KRUSH Tech is an international technology company developing advanced hardware solutions for defense, aerospace, communications, and autonomous systems. We're launching our U.S. operations from the ground up, building a next-generation, vertically integrated aerospace organization focused on advanced uncrewed aircraft systems (UAS), autonomy, and sensing technologies for the U.S. market and strategic partners. Our teams work across RF, embedded systems, electronics, mechanical engineering, software, manufacturing, and supply chain to turn some of the industry's most demanding engineering challenges into reliable, production-ready solutions, combining the agility of a startup with the ambition to compete at the leading edge of UAS and autonomous systems.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a Director of Program Management to lead program delivery for KRUSH's uncrewed aircraft systems, from development through production and fielding. This senior leadership role owns cost, schedule, and technical delivery performance across a portfolio of cross-functional programs, aligns engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and test around clear milestones, and serves as the point of accountability for customers and partners.

Reporting to the Vice President of Manufacturing Operations, you will build program management discipline in a start-up U.S. operation: light enough to move fast, and rigorous enough to meet customer commitments. You will partner closely with engineering and manufacturing leaders to take products from concept through production ramp, balancing competing priorities, risks, and resources across programs.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

* Own cost, schedule, scope, and technical delivery performance across a portfolio of programs, from development through production and fielding
* Develop and implement program management strategy, governance, and standards, using lightweight processes and tools that fit a fast-moving start-up
* Ensure programs align with corporate objectives and strategic priorities, and lead portfolio reviews that prioritize initiatives by business value and strategic impact
* Build, lead, and develop the program management team as the organization grows, including career development and succession planning
* Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, and Test leaders to drive decisions, manage dependencies, and resolve issues across functions
* Lead the transition of programs from development into production, including readiness reviews and stage-gate decisions
* Manage portfolio resource allocation, monitor program performance and interdependencies, and balance competing priorities
* Serve as the primary interface with customers, executive leadership, and external partners, communicating program status, risks, opportunities, and outcomes, and facilitating steering committees and executive reviews
* Develop and manage program budgets and forecasts, monitor financial performance, evaluate business cases and return on investment, and support annual planning and investment prioritization
* Identify, assess, and mitigate program risks and issues, and develop contingency plans for critical risks
* Lead change management and organizational readiness activities for program changes
* Ensure compliance with governance, regulatory, export control, and contractual requirements
* Implement program and portfolio management tools and reporting systems, and define and track program KPIs, including on-time milestone achievement, budget adherence, resource utilization, and risk mitigation effectiveness
* Promote a culture of accountability, transparency, and delivery excellence

 **Requirements**

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field
* 10+ years of program and project management experience, preferably in aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability hardware
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing large programs or a PMO function
* Experience leading cross-functional, hardware-intensive programs from development through production
* Experience managing programs under customer or government contracts, including cost, schedule, and deliverable performance
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional strategic initiatives and to influence executive stakeholders
* Strong skills in program and portfolio management, strategic planning, financial and budget management, risk and issue management, change management, and resource planning
* Strong data analysis and executive reporting skills, with experience in business process improvement
* Strong leadership, negotiation, and influencing skills
* Active U.S. Secret security clearance, with the ability to maintain it
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally up to 50% of the time
* Must qualify as a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities (ITAR)

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

* Master's degree (MBA or equivalent)
* Familiarity with defense contracting and acquisition processes, including FAR/DFARS, contract types, CDRLs, and earned value management
* Experience building a program management function or PMO at a start-up or high-growth company
* PMP or an equivalent program management certification

 **Benefits**

KRUSH Tech offers a competitive compensation package. Compensation is determined by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. Individual offers are determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on interview performance, job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, and internal equity.

The salary range provided is a good faith estimate of the applicable range as of the date of posting. The final offer will be determined after considering all relevant factors, including a candidate's qualifications and experience.

In addition to base pay, KRUSH Tech offers a monthly benefits stipend that employees can apply toward the health, dental, vision, or other coverage that best fits their needs, along with 9 paid federal holidays per year.

**Equal Opportunity Employer**

KRUSH Tech is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace and providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

**Reasonable Accommodation Statement**

KRUSH Tech is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the application and hiring process and during employment. If you require assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please contact Human Resources.

existing_roles.title: Global Director of Quality
existing_roles.description:
**Lead Globally. Drive Innovation. Make an Impact.**

**Join Amphenol Alden and Make a Difference in Patient Care Worldwide!**

At **Amphenol Alden Products (AAP)**, what we do matters. Our medical cable assemblies and interconnect solutions support the advanced technologies healthcare professionals rely on every day. Behind every product is a patient, a family, and an opportunity to make a difference in someone's life.

With roots as a family business more than 90 years ago, Amphenol Alden combines a proud history and entrepreneurial spirit with the resources and opportunities of a global corporation. We are a growing organization that values innovation, teamwork, accountability, and the contributions of our employees.

We believe our people are the foundation of our success. That's why we offer competitive compensation, an outstanding benefits package, work/life balance, and opportunities for professional growth and development.

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking an experienced and strategic **Global Director of Quality** to lead and advance quality operations across four manufacturing facilities in the United States, Mexico, India, and China.

Reporting to AAP’s General Manager and serving as a member of the Leadership Team, this individual will establish and drive the global quality strategy, strengthen Quality Management Systems (QMS), and promote a culture of quality excellence and continuous improvement throughout the organization.

This is an opportunity to make a significant impact by developing high-performing global Quality teams, driving operational improvements, strengthening customer and supplier partnerships, and ensuring consistent quality standards across all manufacturing locations.

**Principal Duties and Responsibilities**

* **Global Quality Strategy:** Develop and execute global quality strategies, objectives, and initiatives that support business goals, product quality, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence.
* **Quality Management Systems:** Lead the development, implementation, standardization, and continuous improvement of Quality Management Systems across all facilities, ensuring compliance with ISO 9001, ISO 13485, applicable FDA requirements, customer specifications, and other relevant regulatory standards.
* **Executive Leadership:** Participate as a member of the Executive Leadership Team in establishing business strategies, operational objectives, and organizational improvement initiatives.
* **Quality Performance:** Establish and monitor global quality metrics, including customer complaints, internal and supplier defects, Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ), corrective actions, and audit performance. Drive measurable improvements in quality and process capability.
* **Continuous Improvement:** Champion Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and data-driven problem-solving methodologies to reduce defects, minimize waste, improve process consistency, and enhance overall operational performance.
* **Engineering and Operations Partnership:** Collaborate with Engineering and Operations to ensure effective quality planning, design and process FMEAs, risk assessments, process validation, and verification throughout the product lifecycle.
* **New Product Introduction:** Provide quality leadership for New Product Introduction (NPI) and manufacturing transfers, ensuring process capability, quality requirements, and customer expectations are met before production release.
* **Supplier Quality:** Partner with Global Supply Chain to develop and maintain a high-performing supplier base through supplier qualification, audits, performance monitoring, development, and corrective action programs.
* **Customer Quality:** Provide strategic leadership for customer quality initiatives, serving as the senior escalation point for significant quality concerns, customer audits, and corrective action resolution.
* **Audits and Regulatory Compliance:** Oversee internal and external quality audits, regulatory inspections, and management reviews, ensuring findings are addressed promptly and compliance is sustained.
* **Corrective and Preventive Action:** Strengthen global CAPA processes through effective root cause analysis, risk mitigation, and prevention of recurring quality issues.
* **Global Team Leadership:** Lead, mentor, and develop the global Quality organization, establishing clear expectations, accountability, talent development plans, and succession strategies.
* **Global Standardization:** Promote consistency and the sharing of best practices across manufacturing facilities in the United States, Mexico, India, and China.
* **Executive Reporting:** Provide regular updates to executive leadership on global quality performance, emerging risks, customer satisfaction, and progress toward strategic quality objectives.

**Related Experience and Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Quality, Engineering, or a related technical or scientific discipline; Master's degree preferred.
* 10+ years of previous related experience and at least 5 years of experience managing individuals.
* Strong knowledge of ISO 13485, ISO 9001, FDA Quality System requirements, and applicable regulatory standards.
* Demonstrated experience leading Quality Management Systems and continuous improvement initiatives across multiple manufacturing locations.
* Strong working knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, CAPA, root cause analysis, risk management, and quality improvement methodologies.
* Proven ability to influence cross-functional teams, develop talent, and drive results in a global organization.

**Why Join Amphenol Alden?**

We believe great people deserve a great place to work. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support your professional success, financial future, and overall well-being.

* Competitive salary and bonus opportunity.
* Hybrid work schedule.
* Excellent 401(k) retirement savings plan to help you plan for the future.
* Comprehensive benefits, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short- and long-term disability, Health Savings Account (HSA), and Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA).
* Employee discounts and company-sponsored activities.
* Opportunities for professional growth and career development.
* The opportunity to lead a global organization and make a meaningful contribution to products that support patient care worldwide.

**Ready to Lead What's Next?**

If you are a strategic quality leader who thrives on building strong teams, solving complex challenges, and driving results across global operations, we'd love to hear from you!

**Join Amphenol Alden and help shape the future of our global operations while making a difference in patient care around the world.**

*Amphenol Alden Products is an Equal Opportunity Employer.*

*Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer sponsorship.*

existing_roles.description:
**About Tutor**

We believe robots should be the next chapter in making physical labor safer and more affordable. But, nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t have a single robot. Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

We build robots that go straight into real factories and warehouses, to do real work, with real impact. Our robot Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Our robot Sonny does handwork, using two arms to achieve human-like dexterity in picking and packing. Every robot learns on the job, and each one we deploy makes the next one more capable, more affordable, and faster to put to work.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, we do it all in-house: the robotics hardware, the machine learning, and the field deployment and service. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

**Why Tutor?**

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

**The Role**

Tutor is hiring a Head of Quality to lead quality as a function, alongside the Head of Manufacturing. You own the quality system, supplier quality across our supply base, product safety certifications, and the quality targets the company holds itself to. The quality engineers and the quality manager report to you, and you grow the team from there. You report to the CTO. As our operations organization grows, you and the Head of Manufacturing will report to the leader of that organization.

This is a building role. The first pieces, incoming inspection, supplier controls and failure analysis, are being put in place by the team you will lead. Your job is to turn them into a system that holds as production grows, a supplier base we can trust, and a quality record that customers and certifying bodies can verify. You have the authority to hold any shipment that is not right.

### **Requirements**

* You have led a quality function at a company that builds complex electromechanical hardware in volume
* You have built or rebuilt a quality system and taken it through ISO 9001 or an equivalent certification
* You have run supplier quality across a supply base, including suppliers overseas
* You have taken a product through product safety certification
* You have built and led a team of quality engineers and managers
* You make decisions from data, and you can hold a shipment when the data says so

### **Nice to haves**

* Robotics, automation, vehicles, or capital equipment
* Reliability engineering methods: life testing, failure rate analysis, design reviews
* Building quality data and tooling that other teams use
* Experience with manufacturing execution systems

### **Benefits**

* **Fully employer-covered health insurance**, so you’re protected without the premium.
* **A managed 401(k)** to help you plan for the future.
* **Generous time off:** unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
* **Regular in-office meals** and team social events throughout the year.

**Compensation**

The base salary range for this role is $220,000 to $280,000, depending on experience.

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

*Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.*

existing_roles.title: Operations Director
existing_roles.description:
Gotion Inc. is based in Silicon Valley, CA, currently building a Manufacturing facility in Manteno, IL and has R&D centers in Ohio, China, Japan and Europe. We innovate in the next generation electric vehicle and energy storage technologies (lithium batteries and related systems) with the aim to accelerate electrified transportation and achieve sustainable development. Gotion is powered by a leading power battery technology company that provides solutions for vehicles including the world's first mass commercial e-bus route. 
 
Gotion is a career destination - we are not simply attempting to just fill another job, but to pursue a dream of global green energy together! We offer outstanding opportunities to individuals seeking an exciting and challenging working environment. Everyone is highly valued and plays a vital role in the growth of our organization.

**Position Summary**

The Operations Director is responsible for leading and coordinating key operational functions of the manufacturing facility, including **Production Planning, Supply Chain, Environmental Health & Safety (EHS), and Infrastructure/Construction Engineering**.

This position plays a critical role in ensuring production readiness, material availability, operational continuity, regulatory compliance, facility development, and cross-functional execution.

The Operations Director will work closely with Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering, Finance, Human Resources, and other functional leaders to support safe, efficient, and scalable operations of the Chicago manufacturing facility.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Production Planning & Operations Coordination**

* Lead production planning and scheduling based on demand, capacity, materials, and priorities.
* Develop and manage short- and long-term production plans.
* Coordinate manpower, equipment, and materials to achieve production targets.
* Monitor plan execution and identify delivery risks.
* Drive cross-functional efforts to resolve production and operational constraints.
* Track key KPIs, including production attainment, inventory, material availability, delivery, and efficiency.
* Support S&OP and capacity planning processes.

* **Supply Chain Management**

* Lead plant supply chain operations, including production planning, materials, procurement, inventory, warehousing, and logistics.
* Ensure material availability while maintaining optimal inventory levels.
* Improve inventory turnover and reduce excess and obsolete stock.
* Drive supplier performance and supply continuity.
* Identify supply chain risks and implement contingency plans.
* Manage domestic and international logistics activities.
* Lead continuous improvement in cost, efficiency, and delivery performance.

* **Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS)**

* Lead the plant's EHS programs and team to ensure compliance with safety and environmental regulations.
* Promote a strong safety culture and drive workplace safety initiatives.
* Oversee inspections, risk assessments, corrective actions, and emergency preparedness.
* Monitor EHS performance and implement corrective actions as needed.
* Partner with cross-functional teams to improve safety and compliance.
* Support regulatory audits, inspections, and permitting activities.

* **Infrastructure & Construction Engineering**

* Lead facility engineering, infrastructure, and construction projects supporting plant operations.
* Oversee plant expansion, renovations, and infrastructure improvements.
* Manage contractors, vendors, and project stakeholders.
* Ensure projects meet scope, budget, schedule, quality, and safety requirements.
* Maintain critical facility systems, utilities, and infrastructure readiness.
* Support production line installation, commissioning, and facility startup activities.

* **Operational Excellence & Cross-Functional Management**

* Establish and manage operational processes across planning, supply chain, EHS, and infrastructure.
* Lead operational reviews and drive action item completion.
* Identify and escalate operational risks to plant leadership.
* Implement continuous improvement initiatives focused on safety, cost, delivery, inventory, and efficiency.
* Drive KPI-based decision-making and operational visibility.
* Support ERP/MRP and digitalization initiatives.
* Foster collaboration across Operations, Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering, Finance, HR, and IT.

* **Team Leadership**

* Lead, develop, and mentor managers and operational teams.
* Establish organizational structure, goals, and succession plans.
* Recruit, develop, and retain key talent.
* Drive performance, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Foster a collaborative, safety-focused, high-performance culture.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field required.
* Master's degree or MBA preferred.
* **10+ years of progressive experience** in manufacturing operations, supply chain, production planning, engineering, or related functions.
* **5+ years of leadership experience** managing managers and/or multiple operational functions.
* Strong experience in large-scale manufacturing environments.
* Demonstrated experience in production planning, supply chain management, and plant operations.
* Working knowledge of EHS management and U.S. regulatory requirements.
* Experience supporting facility construction, plant expansion, infrastructure, or manufacturing engineering projects strongly preferred.
* Strong knowledge of ERP/MRP systems; SAP experience preferred.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in **lithium-ion battery, EV, automotive, energy storage, electronics, or advanced manufacturing**.
* Experience supporting the launch or ramp-up of a new manufacturing facility in the United States.
* Experience managing complex global supply chains.
* Familiarity with high-volume automated manufacturing environments.
* Experience working with international and cross-cultural teams.
* Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, S&OP, inventory optimization, and operational excellence methodologies.
* PMP, APICS/CPIM/CSCP, Six Sigma, or related professional certification is a plus.

**Key Performance Indicators**

Key performance measures may include:

**Production Planning:** Production Plan Attainment | Capacity Utilization | Schedule Adherence

**Supply Chain:** On-Time Delivery | Material Availability | Inventory Turns | Inventory Accuracy | Logistics Cost

**EHS:** Safety Incident Rate | Corrective Action Closure | Regulatory Compliance | Environmental Performance

**Infrastructure:** Project Schedule | Project Budget | Construction Safety | Facility Readiness | Utility Reliability

**Overall Operations:** Cost Reduction | Operational Efficiency | Risk Management | Cross-Functional Execution

**Leadership Scope**

The Operations Director provides leadership and management oversight for:

**Production Planning / PMC**

**Supply Chain & Logistics**

**Warehouse & Inventory**

**Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS)**

**Infrastructure / Construction / Facility Engineering**

existing_roles.description:
Position Overview

We are partnering with an established, innovative manufacturer of advanced semiconductor capital equipment to identify an experienced Director of Manufacturing Operations.

This highly visible leadership position is responsible for overseeing a complex manufacturing organization, driving operational excellence, and ensuring the successful assembly, integration, testing, and delivery of sophisticated capital equipment systems.

The ideal candidate is a decisive, hands-on operations leader who thrives in a fast-paced, technically complex manufacturing environment. This individual will bring a strong sense of ownership and accountability, with the ability to develop high-performing teams, solve challenging operational problems, and consistently deliver against customer commitments.

This role requires a strategic thinker who is equally comfortable managing day-to-day factory execution, driving continuous improvement initiatives, and communicating manufacturing performance, financial results, and operational strategy to executive leadership.

Key Responsibilities

Manufacturing Operations & Execution

* Lead daily manufacturing operations across sub-assembly, system assembly, integration, and final test functions.
* Take direct ownership of manufacturing performance, including on-time shipments, product quality, production schedules, and customer commitments.
* Establish and execute manufacturing strategies aligned with organizational objectives, customer requirements, and business growth.
* Identify and resolve production bottlenecks, resource constraints, and operational challenges to maintain consistent factory output.
* Drive operational accountability through clearly defined performance metrics, structured problem-solving, and decisive leadership.
* Ensure manufacturing capacity, staffing, and production resources are aligned with business demand.

Financial & Operational Management

* Develop and manage manufacturing operating budgets, resource plans, labor utilization, and production costs.
* Monitor and communicate key financial and operational metrics, including manufacturing output, revenue-related shipment performance, labor overhead, operating expenses, and production capacity.
* Present manufacturing performance, operational risks, and improvement initiatives to senior executive leadership.
* Identify opportunities to improve cost efficiency, resource utilization, and overall manufacturing productivity.
* Support strategic business planning through accurate capacity assessments, operational forecasting, and data-driven decision-making.

Leadership & Organizational Development

* Lead, mentor, and develop a manufacturing organization consisting of production managers, supervisors, engineers, technicians, and operational support personnel.
* Establish a culture of accountability, ownership, urgency, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* Evaluate organizational capabilities, identify leadership gaps, and implement development plans to strengthen management effectiveness.
* Make timely, well-informed decisions to address performance issues, operational challenges, and organizational needs.
* Build a high-performance manufacturing culture focused on execution, safety, quality, and customer satisfaction.
* Promote effective cross-functional collaboration with engineering, quality, supply chain, and executive leadership.

Quality & Continuous Improvement

* Champion a proactive safety culture and ensure compliance with applicable manufacturing safety and quality standards.
* Drive improvements in product quality, first-pass yield, manufacturing consistency, and customer satisfaction.
* Lead structured root-cause investigations and corrective action initiatives using methodologies such as 8D, Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and statistical process control.
* Develop and execute continuous improvement roadmaps focused on cycle-time reduction, process efficiency, waste elimination, and operational scalability.
* Implement proactive quality initiatives that identify and resolve manufacturing issues earlier in the production process.
* Maintain compliance with applicable ISO certifications and established quality management systems.

Manufacturing Engineering & Process Optimization

* Partner with engineering and manufacturing teams to improve product manufacturability, assembly efficiency, and test effectiveness.
* Drive improvements in manufacturing test strategies, including modular testing, parallel test execution, and automated test methods.
* Identify opportunities to reduce final system test cycle times while maintaining rigorous product quality standards.
* Support new product introductions, engineering changes, and production transitions to ensure manufacturing readiness.
* Collaborate with global suppliers and contract manufacturing partners to support production requirements and operational objectives.
* Lead manufacturing-related insourcing, outsourcing, and production transfer initiatives as required.

Required Qualifications

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Operations Management, or a related technical discipline.
* Minimum of 5 years of progressively responsible experience in manufacturing or operations, including at least 5 years in a manufacturing operations leadership role within the semiconductor capital equipment industry.
* Demonstrated experience managing complex capital equipment manufacturing operations, including assembly, integration, testing, and final product delivery.
* Proven accountability for factory performance, production output, on-time shipments, manufacturing quality, and operational execution.
* Strong financial and business acumen, including experience managing manufacturing budgets, labor costs, overhead, capacity planning, and production-related financial performance.
* Ability to communicate operational results, financial performance, manufacturing risks, and strategic recommendations effectively to executive leadership.
* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing teams and developing managers in a demanding, high-performance environment.
* Strong knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, structured problem-solving, quality management systems, and data-driven operational improvement.
* Decisive leadership style with a demonstrated ability to solve problems, make difficult decisions, and drive accountability across an organization.

Preferred Qualifications

* Experience manufacturing sophisticated semiconductor processing or precision capital equipment systems.
* Experience leading manufacturing organizations of approximately 100 employees, including multiple direct-report managers.
* Demonstrated success implementing Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Value Stream Mapping, and continuous improvement programs.
* Experience with SAP, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), and advanced manufacturing analytics tools.
* Proven success reducing manufacturing cycle times, improving production throughput, and implementing automated or modular final test strategies.
* Experience applying Design for Manufacturability (DfM) principles in collaboration with engineering and product development teams.
* Experience supporting international supply chains, global supplier relationships, and contract manufacturing operations.
* Familiarity with new product introduction, manufacturing transfer, and production scalability initiatives.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The successful candidate will be a confident, results-oriented manufacturing leader who combines strong technical manufacturing knowledge with exceptional operational discipline and business judgment.

This individual should have a proven track record of leading complex semiconductor capital equipment (low-volume/high-mix) manufacturing organizations, improving factory performance, and developing accountable, high-performing teams.

They must be comfortable operating at both the strategic and tactical levels—whether presenting operational and financial performance to executive leadership, making critical production decisions, resolving manufacturing challenges, or coaching managers to improve execution.

Above all, this role requires a leader who takes ownership, drives decisions, holds teams accountable, and consistently delivers measurable operational results.

Additional Information

* Onsite leadership position based in San Jose, California.
* Occasional domestic and international travel may be required.
* Opportunity to lead a technically sophisticated manufacturing organization with significant visibility and influence across the business.

existing_roles.title: Director of Planning and Production Coordination
existing_roles.description:
**POSITION:** Director of Planning and Production Coordination

**SHIFT:** Monday - Friday, 8:00 am - 5:00 pm + Additional hours based on business demand

**SALARY:** $139,362 - $155,161.50 + (DOE) + Full Benefits Package

**LOCATION: On-site in office in Fargo, ND**

### **SUMMARY OF RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Director of Planning and Production Coordination leads enterprise planning and production coordination across CSP, Tank and Structural product lines. The role establishes consistent planning standards, aligns demand with capacity, ensures production readiness, balances workloads across sites and supports reliable customer commitments. The role owns the planning system and coordination processes.

### **ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS**

* Embrace and demonstrate the qualities of the TrueNorth Steel Game Changer definition.
* Comply with all safety, quality, environmental and workplace requirements.
* Lead, coach, and develop the CSP, Tank and Structural Planning Leaders and the Production Coordinator Supervisor, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and succession coverage.
* Establish and continuously improve an integrated planning and production-coordination system with common standards, planning horizons, terminology, decision rights, data requirements, and escalation paths.
* Align customer demand, forecasts, backlog, inventory, labor, equipment, material availability, and site capability into executable production plans.
* Confirm customer commit-date feasibility using verified readiness, material, capacity, outside-processing, site, and delivery information.
* Provide an enterprise view of capacity and constraints, leading approved workload-balancing actions such as site transfers, priority changes, outsourcing, overtime, and staffing adjustments.
* Define and enforce production-readiness requirements for drawings, bills of material, routing, material, CNC and nesting information, quality requirements, outside services, job packets, shipping information, and approvals.
* Lead regular site, product-line, and enterprise planning reviews that surface demand, capacity, backlog, readiness, schedule performance, risks, and decisions requiring action.
* Partner with Manufacturing, Sales, Project Management, Estimating, Drafting, Engineering, Purchasing, Inventory Control, Quality, Shipping, Logistics, Finance, and other functions to resolve planning constraints.
* Govern planning and production coordination data and transactions in SyteLine, Tekla and other approved systems, including capacity assumptions, work-center data, production status, and readiness information.
* Define performance measures and dashboards for schedule, backlog, capacity, readiness, equipment use, changes, and failure-related costs. Use data to improve delivery, throughput, material utilization, and profitability.
* Establish repeatable standard work, documentation, training, cross-training, and backup coverage to reduce dependence on individual knowledge.
* Serve as the escalation point for significant cross-site, cross-product, and cross-functional planning issues. Elevate unresolved matters with facts, alternatives, risks, and recommendations.
* Support annual business, capacity, capital, workforce, and budget planning, along with strategic manufacturing initiatives.
* Provide the VP of Manufacturing with regular updates on planning risks, delivery, capacity, material, organizational needs, trends, and recommended actions.
* Travel to manufacturing sites is required to understand processes, build relationships, support teams, and ensure consistent implementation of planning and production-coordination standards.
* Prompt and dependable attendance.
* Other duties as assigned.

### **KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND QUALITIES**

* Strong knowledge of manufacturing planning, scheduling, capacity management, production coordination, inventory, and shop-floor execution.
* Ability to lead leaders and standardize planning processes across multiple manufacturing sites or business units.
* Working knowledge of ERP-supported planning, bills of material, routing, work centers, job release, inventory, and production transactions.
* Strong analytical judgment and ability to balance customer commitments, manufacturing capability, cost, and business risk.
* Effective communication, facilitation, change leadership and cross-functional influence skills.
* High integrity, accountability, attention to detail, sound judgment, and bias toward action.
* Commitment to safety, quality, customer service, teamwork, and continuous improvement.

### **EDUCATION AND WORK EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor’s degree in Operations Management, Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Manufacturing, Business Administration, Construction Management or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience.
* Minimum of ten years of progressive responsible experience in manufacturing operations, planning, scheduling, supply chain, project coordination, or a related field preferred, including five years of leadership experience.
* Experience leading multi-site planning or operational processes, ERP-supported planning and cross-functional improvement preferred.
