existing_roles.title: Plant Manager III
existing_roles.description:
EnerSys is a global leader in stored energy solutions helping industrial, infrastructure and defense customers address critical power and operational needs. The company delivers integrated solutions that combine energy storage technologies, power electronics, software-enabled intelligence, technical expertise and comprehensive global customer support. EnerSys supports customers across communications networks, data centers, energy infrastructure, material handling, transportation, aerospace and defense — including applications where power continuity is essential. Serving customers in more than 100 countries, EnerSys helps organizations manage energy more reliably, efficiently and intelligently in complex operating environments where uptime, safety and resilience matter.

 

**Job Purpose**
---------------

The Plant Manager will provide overall leadership for the phased development, start-up, ramp-up, and ongoing operation of the new lithium-ion cell manufacturing facility in Greenville, South Carolina. This is a unique opportunity to build a factory and its organization from the ground up in a fast-paced, highly dynamic environment.

The role will evolve through multiple phases of the project, beginning with facility construction and operational readiness and progressing through equipment installation and commissioning, production launch, workforce ramp-up, stabilization, and full-scale manufacturing operations.

The Plant Manager will be accountable for establishing the operating model, leadership capability, organizational structure, culture, management systems, and performance disciplines required to achieve excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, people, and customer satisfaction.

This leader must bring broad manufacturing expertise in a high-volume, fully automated environment and understand the interdependencies across production, engineering, maintenance, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, finance, and people. The successful candidate will combine strong operational and financial acumen with knowledge of lithium-ion cell manufacturing and a demonstrated ability to build organizations, develop leaders, anticipate workforce needs, and establish strong relationships with employees, customers, suppliers, and business partners.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**
-----------------------------------------

**Factory Development, Start-Up & Operational Readiness**

* Provide operational leadership throughout the phased development of the Greenville facility, ensuring manufacturing and operational requirements are incorporated as the factory is constructed, commissioned, launched, and scaled.
* Partner with Engineering, Project Management, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, EHS, People & Culture, IT/OT, and other functions to establish comprehensive manufacturing readiness.
* Translate facility and project milestones into executable operational plans covering equipment, processes, workforce, training, materials, systems, safety, quality, and infrastructure.
* Ensure equipment, manufacturing processes, systems, organizational capability, and workforce readiness progress together so that potential gaps are identified and resolved before they impact production.
* Establish the operating systems, standard work, governance, performance metrics, escalation processes, and accountability required to transition successfully from project execution into manufacturing operations.
* Lead the operational transition through equipment installation and commissioning, qualification, production launch, ramp-up, stabilization, and full-scale operations.

**Manufacturing & Operational Leadership**

* Provide end-to-end leadership of plant operations with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, capacity, employee performance, and overall manufacturing results.
* Maintain a comprehensive understanding of plant operating processes and ensure effective integration across production, maintenance, engineering, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, and supporting functions.
* Establish a culture of operational excellence, disciplined execution, accountability, continuous improvement, and structured problem solving.
* Establish and continuously evaluate plant KPIs to identify performance gaps, determine root causes, and drive sustainable corrective actions.
* Drive improvement in manufacturing productivity, equipment effectiveness, reliability, throughput, yield, quality, labor efficiency, and operating cost.
* Ensure appropriate manufacturing systems, controls, procedures, and escalation mechanisms are established as production volume and organizational complexity increase.
* Champion Lean manufacturing principles and create a culture in which continuous improvement is embedded throughout the organization.

**Lithium-Ion Cell Manufacturing**

* Provide leadership within a technically complex lithium-ion cell manufacturing environment.
* Apply practical knowledge of cell manufacturing processes, automated manufacturing equipment, process controls, materials, quality requirements, and production risks to operational decision-making.
* Work closely with Cell Engineering, Process Engineering, Quality, EHS, and other technical teams to establish safe, repeatable, high-quality manufacturing processes capable of operating at scale.
* Ensure plant teams understand the relationships among process capability, product quality, yield, throughput, equipment performance, manufacturing cost, and customer requirements.
* Support the effective introduction, industrialization, and scale-up of new manufacturing processes and technologies.

**Financial & Business Leadership**
-----------------------------------

* Own plant operating performance from both an operational and financial perspective.
* Develop and manage plant operating budgets, forecasts, labor plans, productivity targets, capital requirements, and cost-improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrate strong understanding of the economic drivers of manufacturing and translate operational performance into financial and business outcomes.
* Partner closely with Finance to understand and manage manufacturing cost, labor, productivity, inventory, scrap, yield, capital utilization, and other key plant performance drivers.
* Evaluate significant operational decisions through both manufacturing and financial lenses, balancing immediate execution requirements with the long-term capability and competitiveness of the plant.
* Establish strong cost-management and financial disciplines as the facility transitions from construction and start-up investment to sustainable manufacturing operations.

**Workforce Planning & Organizational Capability**

* Build the plant organization in phases aligned with facility construction, commissioning, production launch, ramp-up, and future operating requirements.
* Develop short- and long-term workforce plans to ensure the plant has the appropriate leadership, technical, skilled-trades, professional, and manufacturing capabilities required at each stage of growth.
* Anticipate talent, capacity, skill, and leadership gaps before they become constraints to manufacturing performance or future growth.
* Partner closely with People & Culture to develop recruiting, workforce planning, onboarding, training, retention, employee engagement, talent management, and organizational capability strategies.
* Establish clear organizational structures, decision rights, accountabilities, and leadership responsibilities as the facility grows and becomes operational.
* Develop workforce flexibility and organizational depth to mitigate single points of dependency and ensure business continuity.
* Regularly assess whether workforce capacity and capability are appropriately aligned with production requirements, operating plans, and future growth.

**Leadership Development & Succession**

* Recruit, build, coach, and develop a high-performing plant leadership team capable of successfully operating at increasing levels of scale and complexity.
* Establish a leadership culture where leaders are expected not only to deliver results but also to develop other leaders and build capability within their organizations.
* Partner with People & Culture to regularly assess leadership capability, organizational effectiveness, succession coverage, bench strength, and future talent requirements.
* Build strong succession pipelines for critical plant leadership and technical positions and ensure appropriate development plans are established for potential successors.
* Identify and develop high-potential talent through coaching, mentoring, expanded responsibilities, cross-functional experience, and targeted development opportunities.
* Establish sufficient leadership and technical depth to minimize organizational vulnerability and ensure continuity as the facility grows.
* Create a culture where talent development and succession planning are ongoing leadership responsibilities rather than periodic HR activities.

**Customer, Supplier & Stakeholder Leadership**
-----------------------------------------------

* Build strong, credible, long-term relationships with customers and ensure plant execution consistently supports quality, delivery, responsiveness, and customer commitments.
* Build strategic relationships with suppliers, equipment manufacturers, contractors, and other external partners critical to the construction, start-up, and ongoing operation of the plant.
* Work collaboratively with customers and suppliers to resolve issues quickly while protecting long-term business relationships.
* Serve as a senior representative of the Greenville operation with business leadership, customers, suppliers, community stakeholders, and other external partners as appropriate.
* Build strong cross-functional relationships across the broader organization and effectively navigate a complex, matrixed environment.
* Maintain a visible leadership presence throughout the plant and foster an employee environment built on communication, engagement, trust, accountability, and strong employee relations.

**Safety, Quality & Culture**

* Establish safety as a foundational operating principle and ensure appropriate systems, behaviors, and leadership accountability are embedded throughout the facility.
* Champion a quality-first mindset and ensure the organization consistently meets internal requirements and customer expectations.
* Build a high-performance culture characterized by accountability, collaboration, transparency, urgency, ownership, and continuous improvement.
* Establish clear expectations for leadership behavior and ensure those expectations cascade throughout the plant organization.
* Create an environment where employees understand how their work contributes to plant performance, customer success, and the broader business.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Business, or a related discipline.
* Significant progressive leadership experience within complex, high-volume, highly automated, or advanced manufacturing environments.
* Demonstrated experience leading a significant manufacturing operation with accountability across safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, people, and financial performance.
* Demonstrated experience supporting or leading the build and start-up of a new manufacturing facility, significant plant expansion, major manufacturing transformation, or complex production ramp-up.
* Strong knowledge of lithium-ion cell manufacturing or relevant advanced manufacturing technologies and processes.
* Broad understanding of manufacturing operations and the interdependencies among production, engineering, maintenance, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, finance, and people.
* Strong financial and commercial acumen with experience managing operating budgets, forecasts, manufacturing costs, capital investments, productivity, and business performance.
* Demonstrated success building, leading, coaching, and developing high-performing leadership teams.
* Experience with workforce planning, organizational design, talent development, and leadership succession.
* Demonstrated ability to build effective relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, executive leadership, and cross-functional partners.
* Proven ability to lead through ambiguity and rapidly changing priorities within a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
* Direct experience in lithium-ion cell manufacturing or large-scale battery manufacturing.
* Experience taking a newly constructed manufacturing facility through commissioning, production launch, volume ramp-up, and stabilized operations.
* Experience with highly automated manufacturing equipment and advanced manufacturing technologies.
* Strong working knowledge of Lean manufacturing, structured problem solving, operational excellence, and continuous-improvement methodologies.
* Experience working within a global manufacturing organization or complex matrixed business environment.

**General Job Requirements**
----------------------------

* This position requires working in a plant/warehouse environment. Therefore, expect varying working conditions.

existing_roles.title: Senior Manager, Fulfillment and Logistics Operations, Ford Energy
existing_roles.description:
**Overview**
------------

At Ford, you’ll work on ideas that matter, alongside passionate people who want to make a global impact. Together, we’re shaping the next era of transportation—grounded in purpose, driven by progress. Make your move.

* Job Type: Full time
* Work Type: Hybrid

 

We made history and now we work to transform the future – for our customers, our communities and our families. You'll see your work on the road every day, helping people move freely and pursue their dreams. At Ford, you can build more than vehicles. Come build what matters.

 

Ford Energy is a newly formed, wholly-owned subsidiary of Ford Motor Company dedicated to accelerating U.S. energy independence. Leveraging Ford’s century of manufacturing excellence and world-class battery energy storage systems (BESS) technology, Ford Energy designs, manufactures, and services grid-scale and commercial DC battery energy storage systems (BESS). Ford Energy is uniquely positioned to capture the growing demand for reliable, US-built energy storage systems. We are not just building batteries; we are building the infrastructure for the next generation of the American grid.

Why Ford Energy?

At Ford Energy, you have the backing of an industrial manufacturing powerhouse with the agility of a dedicated energy startup offering industry leading technology. We offer a competitive compensation package including performance-based bonuses, Ford vehicle discounts, and the opportunity to shape the energy strategy of one of the world's most iconic brands.

**In this position...**

The Senior Manager, Fulfillment & Logistics Operations is a senior leadership role accountable for the end-to-end fulfillment, logistics, and parts supply performance of the Project Operations & Performance value stream. This leader sets the direction for inventory and supply planning, parts replenishment, warehousing, distribution, and outbound product shipping, and owns the service, cost, and working capital outcomes of the network. The role also delivers the digital capabilities that give customers real-time visibility into parts inventory, order status, and shipment information, making fulfillment a differentiator in the customer experience. Partnering with Product Creation & Industrialization, Finance, Sales, and Procurement, this leader combines deep supply chain and logistics expertise with change leadership and the ability to build high-performing teams, delivering measurable business impact. [Scope: add annual logistics and inventory spend, number of facilities and 3PL partners, and team size.]

**What you'll do...**

**1. Strategy & Transformation**
 

* Own the fulfillment and logistics strategy across the Project Operations & Performance value stream, aligned with growth and customer experience goals.
* Lead transformation from concept to measurable results, including integration with Product Creation & Industrialization.
* Champion the Voice of Customer, resolve issues quickly, and incorporate insights into product, service, and fulfillment improvements.

**2. Parts Supply, Inventory & Warehousing**
 

* Lead end-to-end spare parts planning, inventory, and distribution, balancing availability, cost-to-serve, and working capital.
* Optimize inventory through segment-specific safety stock and reorder strategies, procurement controls, and clearance of slow-moving stock.
* Hold warehouse partners accountable for inventory accuracy, productivity, and safety.
* Partner with Finance to improve inventory velocity and the cash conversion cycle.

**3. Outbound Logistics & Delivery**
 

* Own delivery performance from factory release to customer or site, establishing service targets and driving perfect-order execution.
* Manage carrier, freight forwarder, and 3PL relationships, including contracts, rates, capacity, mode selection, and performance reviews.
* Ensure battery energy storage shipments meet hazardous materials and oversize/overweight transport requirements, including DOT, packaging, labeling, documentation, and permits.
* Coordinate production, shipping, installation, and site readiness across Sales, Manufacturing, Customer Project Teams, and Finance; resolve delays, damage claims, and exceptions.
* Reduce freight costs and lead times through route optimization, load consolidation, and standardized, system-integrated workflows.

**4. Digital Capabilities & Customer Visibility**
 

* Deliver customer self-service access to parts availability, consumption, order status, shipment tracking, and estimated delivery.
* Partner with IT, Product, and Sales to connect ERP, planning, warehouse, and carrier data through customer portals and API/EDI integrations.
* Provide proactive alerts for delays, backorders, and delivery changes; measure adoption, satisfaction, and reductions in order-status inquiries.
* Replace manual processes with automated workflows using SAP, advanced planning systems, and integrated data.

**5. Supplier & Production Alignment**
 

* Partner with Procurement to monitor Tier 1 and Tier 2 supplier performance and mitigate material risks before they disrupt production.
* Align factory priorities with high-value customer orders and strategic inventory needs.

**6. Leadership, Performance & Continuous Improvement**
 

* Build and develop a high-performing fulfillment, logistics, and supply chain team.
* Present performance, risks, and investment cases to senior leadership and align cross-functional stakeholders.
* Own KPIs such as OTIF, forecast accuracy, inventory turns, backorders, fill rate, lead time, and cost-to-serve; quantify the financial and operational impact of improvements.
* Improve service and field performance through shorter repair cycles, higher first-time-fix rates, and greater product reliability.
* Lead change adoption and apply Lean and Six Sigma methods to eliminate waste and reduce fulfillment lead times.

**You'll have...**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations, Business Administration, or at least 10 years' of experience in a related field
* 8+ years of progressive experience in aftermarket operations, service supply chain, fulfillment, or logistics, including leading managers and multi-functional teams.
* Proven record of leading large-scale operational or digital transformation initiatives across multi-functional teams.
* Deep expertise in spare parts planning, inventory management, warehousing, distribution, and outbound logistics.
* Financial acumen, including budget ownership and working capital management.
* Executive-level communication and influencing skills, with the ability to partner with and present to stakeholders at all levels.
* Must be able to travel 50% as needed

**Even better, you'll have...**

* Master's Degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or APICS CPIM certification is a plus.
* Experience in the automotive or heavy equipment aftermarket/service industry.
* Experience delivering customer-facing digital capabilities, such as portals, order and shipment visibility tools, or API/EDI integrations.
* Experience in transportation, outbound logistics, or freight management, including hazardous materials or oversize/overweight shipping.
* Knowledge of project management methodologies (e.g., Agile).
* Experience working with Salesforce and/or SAP S4 HANA.
* Experience in high-mix, global manufacturing or consumer/industrial industries.

**Additional Information:**

Work Location: Dearborn or Kentucky (United States), but the company is willing to consider a hybrid modality

Required Travel: Up to 50% travel required

You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you think you can bring value to Ford Motor Company, we encourage you to apply!

As an established global company, we offer the benefit of choice. You can choose what your Ford future will look like: will your story span the globe, or keep you close to home? Will your career be a deep dive into what you love, or a series of new teams and new skills? Will you be a leader, a changemaker, a technical expert, a culture builder…or all of the above? No matter what you choose, we offer a work life that works for you, including:
 

* Immediate medical, dental, vision and prescription drug coverage
* Flexible family care days, paid parental leave, new parent ramp-up programs, subsidized back-up child care and more
* Family building benefits including adoption and surrogacy expense reimbursement, fertility treatments, and more
* Vehicle discount program for employees and family members and management leases
* Tuition assistance
* Established and active employee resource groups
* Paid time off for individual and team community service
* A generous schedule of paid holidays, including the week between Christmas and New Year’s Day
* Paid time off and the option to purchase additional vacation time.

This position is leadership level 5 and ranges from $141,700-$268,300.

Final determination of salary grade will be based on candidate's skills and experience, and base salary will be set within the applicable range according to job scope, responsibility and competitive market value.

For more information on salary and benefits, click here: https://fordcareers.co/LL5

For more information on salary and benefits, click here: https://fordcareers.co/GSR

Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Candidates for positions with Ford Motor Company must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required at the time of hire.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, age, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability status or protected veteran status. In the United States, if you need a reasonable accommodation for the online application process due to a disability, please call 1-888-336-0660.

protected_roles.title: Director, Evaluation and Quality Assurance, Services Special Projects
protected_roles.description:
Summary
 
 
We are looking for a Director to build and lead the evaluation and quality assurance function for one of our most ambitious multi-year engineering initiatives. This is a true 0-to-1, first-key-hire role: There is no existing team, tooling, or process to inherit. You will define how we measure quality across an entire product end to end, build the automation and evaluation infrastructure to do it at scale (or borrow other teams' infrastructure), and build and lead the organization that runs it.
 
 
Description
 
 
You will own evaluation and quality assurance for every layer of the product — from whether the system is being correctly triggered for the right set of user requests, through whether it surfaces and ranks the right results, to whether the underlying transactions execute correctly, including integrations with external partner APIs, and financial systems. Quality here isn't a single test suite — it spans conversational understanding, relevance and ranking, and revenue-bearing correctness, all against a large, constantly evolving real-world dataset. You will create and drive the evaluation and quality strategy and implementation for the product. This will extensively utilize automated grading systems and human evaluation programs where appropriate. You will make the calls about where to invest in each. You will define what "correct" and "good" mean for this product, wire that definition into continuous, always-on evaluation pipelines with clear pass/fail quality gates tied to releases, and build the team, tooling, and operating rhythm to catch issues before they reach users. As the first hire in this space, you will operate with significant latitude and ambiguity — setting strategy, process, and technical direction with minimal existing scaffolding, while also building and scaling an organization. You will partner closely with engineering, applied ML, and program management leadership, including senior executive stakeholders, and you will be a key voice in defining what "done" and "shippable" mean for a product still taking shape, as well as iterating on decision points in production after the product ships.
 
 
Minimum Qualifications 
 
 

* 12+ years of experience in data science, machine learning evaluation, quality assurance, or test engineering roles in a technical product environment, including experience building and leading multi-level QA or evaluation organizations through managers.
* Demonstrated experience building an evaluation or QA function from the ground up — defining metrics, process, tooling, and organizational structure where none previously existed.
* Extensive experience utilizing LLM-based autograders and rubrics, including rubric design, evaluation set development, validation, calibration, and human-model alignment, and using them to proactively drive product and model improvements.
* Deep experience in traditional human evaluation methodology, logging, and A/B testing for consumer-facing products at scale.
* Experience evaluating conversational AI, recommendation, ranking, or search systems, and — ideally — agentic or tool-use systems that take real-world actions, not just generate responses.
* BS in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.
* Experience with quality assurance for third-party API integrations.
* Experience with logging infrastructure and instrumentation for AI product quality measurement.
* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of presenting quality status, risk, and trade-offs clearly to, and influencing decisions among, senior executive leadership.

 
 
 
Preferred Qualifications 
 
 

* 15+ years of experience in data science, machine learning evaluation, quality assurance, or test engineering roles in a technical product environment, including experience building and leading multi-level QA or evaluation organizations through managers.

 
 
 
At Apple, base pay is one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range. This provides the opportunity to progress as you grow and develop within a role. The base pay range for this role is between $311,100 and $496,900, and your base pay will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. 
 
Apple employees also have the opportunity to become an Apple shareholder through participation in Apple’s discretionary employee stock programs. Apple employees are eligible for discretionary restricted stock unit awards, and can purchase Apple stock at a discount if voluntarily participating in Apple’s Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You’ll also receive benefits including: Comprehensive medical and dental coverage, retirement benefits, a range of discounted products and free services, and for formal education related to advancing your career at Apple, reimbursement for certain educational expenses — including tuition. Additionally, this role might be eligible for discretionary bonuses or commission payments as well as relocation. Learn more about Apple Benefits 
 
Note: Apple benefit, compensation and employee stock programs are subject to eligibility requirements and other terms of the applicable plan or program. 
 
 

Apple is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to inclusion and diversity. We seek to promote equal opportunity for all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, Veteran status, or other legally protected characteristics. Learn more about your EEO rights as an applicant

 
 
 

At Apple, we believe accessibility is a fundamental human right. You’ll find that idea reflected in everything here — in our culture, our benefits and our digital tools. By welcoming as many perspectives as possible, we help you build a career where you feel like you belong. 
 
Learn about accessibility in Apple’s workplace 
 
Learn about reasonable accommodations for job applicants

 
 
 

Apple accepts applications to this posting on an ongoing basis.

protected_roles.title: Director, Quality
protected_roles.description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We’re looking for a Director, Quality to lead quality strategy and execution across Oura’s global engineering organization and supply chain.

### **What You Will Do:**

* In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
* You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
* This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
* Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
* Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
* Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
* Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
* Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
* Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
* Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
* Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
* Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.
* Lead launch and ramp readiness: Review product and component qualification, supplier capability, manufacturing readiness, validation evidence, yield, open risks, reliability results, and corrective actions before launch and ramp decisions.
* Govern quality-related changes: Ensure design, material, component, supplier, process, software, and manufacturing changes are evaluated for quality and reliability impact and implemented consistently through ECR/ECN and change-control processes.
* Establish a data-driven quality operating system: Define leading and lagging indicators across development, suppliers, manufacturing, and the field. Improve data quality, traceability, dashboards, and escalation mechanisms.
* Drive continuous improvement: Reduce defects, escapes, returns, warranty claims, rework, scrap, and other sources of cost of poor quality while improving product reliability, supplier performance, and customer experience.
* Influence cross-functional decisions: Provide clear, risk-based recommendations when quality, schedule, cost, performance, capacity, and supply continuity priorities compete.
* Communicate with senior leadership: Present concise assessments of product risk, supplier and manufacturing performance, launch readiness, field quality, and improvement priorities.
* Build a culture of prevention and accountability: Make quality a shared responsibility across engineering and operations, with clear ownership for requirements, validation, supplier controls, manufacturing execution, and sustained performance.

This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

### **What you'll bring**

* 15+ years of experience in product quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, operations quality, or a related engineering discipline, including significant people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success leading quality for complex, high-volume consumer electronics, wearable, medical-adjacent, or similarly reliability-sensitive products.
* Experience leading and developing teams across one or more of the following areas: product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, or sustaining quality.
* A track record of establishing quality strategy, operating mechanisms, and measurable improvements from early product development through launch and sustaining.
* Strong understanding of product development, design verification and validation, component qualification, reliability engineering, supplier quality, manufacturing processes, and production ramp.
* Strong command of quality and problem-solving methods, including FMEA, 8D, CAPA, SPC, GR&R, DOE, root-cause analysis, control plans, and process capability.
* Experience using engineering, field, warranty, customer support, supplier, and manufacturing data to identify systemic risks and drive corrective action.
* Demonstrated ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, and executive leadership without relying solely on direct authority.
* Experience with engineering change control, supplier changes, component qualification, process validation, manufacturing readiness, or production quality improvement.
* Strong understanding of DFM/DFA, GD&T, Lean and Six Sigma principles, measurement systems, and quality management systems.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical risks into concise decisions and actions.
* A self-directed, pragmatic, and resilient leadership style, with a willingness to engage deeply in details while maintaining a strategic perspective.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Systems, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field required; advanced degree or quality certification is a plus.
* Preferred qualifications
* Experience with both product quality and supplier or manufacturing quality, or demonstrated ability to operate effectively across both domains.
* Experience with batteries, electronics, sensors, RF systems, precision mechanics, adhesives, miniaturized assemblies, or other demanding product technologies.
* Experience leading quality for products that combine hardware, firmware, software, and cloud-enabled member experiences.
* Experience building or scaling quality management systems during rapid company growth.
* Familiarity with product safety, regulatory, compliance, traceability, and risk-management requirements relevant to wearable technology.
* Experience with supplier development, APQP, PPAP, SCAR processes, multi-source strategies, capacity expansion, or major manufacturing transitions.
* Experience working across multiple countries, engineering sites, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

### **Nice to have:**

* HW Experience
* Global distributor teams
* grown and org

### **Benefits**

At Ōura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Ōura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health.

What we offer:

* Competitive salary and equity packages
* Health, dental, vision insurance, and mental health resources
* An Ōura Ring of your own plus employee discounts for friends & family
* 20 days of paid time off plus 13 paid holidays plus 8 days of flexible wellness time off
* Paid sick leave and parental leave

Ōura takes a market-based approach to pay, which may vary depending on your location. US locations are categorized into tiers based on a cost of labor index for that geographic area. While most offers will be closer to the starting range, successful candidates' pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location, internal peer equity, and market conditions. These ranges may be modified in the future.

Region 2 $MIN- $MID
 
Region 3 $MIN- $MID

A recruiter can determine your Region based on your US location.

We are not considering candidates residing in the following states: Alaska (AK), Delaware (DE), Iowa (IA), Mississippi (MS), Nebraska (NE), South Dakota (SD), West Virginia (WV), and Wisconsin (WI).

ŌURA is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Individuals seeking employment at ŌURA are considered without regard to age, ancestry, color, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, mental or physical disability, national origin, protected family care or medical leave status, race, religion (including beliefs and practices or the absence thereof), sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. We will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics.

We will work to ensure individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment.

Disclaimer: Beware of fake job offers!
 
We’ve been alerted to scammers posing as ŌURA recruiters, especially for remote roles. Please note:

* Our jobs are listed only on the ŌURA Careers page and trusted job boards.
* We will never ask for personal information like ID or payment for equipment upfront.
* Official offers are sent through Docusign after a verbal offer, not via text or email.

Stay cautious and protect your personal details.

protected_roles.description:
**Lassonde Pappas & Co.** is a US Leader in beverage manufacturing dedicated to our team members, customers and consumers satisfaction. We remain committed to our small-town roots and rural values. **Hardworking** and **caring** are qualities that make our teams special. Since 1942, we’ve been producing delicious products for our customers across the country!

To provide the best for our customers, we focus on building the best team by creating and advancing an inclusive environment amongst our diverse workforces. If you’re passionate about customer satisfaction, reliable, and committed to being and doing better, join us!

**We value each of our employees’ total wellbeing. To support employees in all stages of their wellness journey, we have a robust benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage options, growth and development potential, along with 401-K, Life & Disability Insurance, PTO, Tuition Reimbursement, Health Fairs, Gym Membership Discounts, and so much more!**

*Pay Range for this position is: $155,000-$200,000 plus annual bonus, depending on experience and geographical location.*

**POSITION SUMMARY** 
The Environmental Health and Safety Director leads the development, implementation, and performance of health, safety, and environmental programs and policies at Lassonde Pappas & Co. Inc. facilities, to maintain compliance with applicable national and local regulations and to ensure a safe, healthy working environment for all employees. This role reports to the VP of Manufacturing for the US and is based out of our Cherry Hill, New Jersey location.

**Primary Responsibilities include*****:***

* Oversee and ensure the organization’s compliance with local, state, and federal environment, health, and safety regulations including (but not limited to) fire safety and OSHA regulations, and keep up with any changes to laws and regulations that impact the organization
* Work closely with the organization’s legal department to ensure that the company is in compliance with these regulations
* Direct audits and work with each plant and its departments to ensure that all company guidelines are being followed
* Manage the safety budget at the manufacturing sites to ensure that appropriate personal protective and safety equipment is available as needed to prevent injuries and provide for a safe and healthy work environment
* Develop, implement, and evaluate programs, policies, and procedures related to health, safety, and environmental issues in the workplace, and ensure that environmental policy and procedure manuals are available and updated at all times to reduce the risk of injury or illness in the workplace
* Prepare, schedule, and execute training to cover emergency procedures, workplace safety, and other relevant topics
* Lead the planning, execution, monitoring and continuous improvement of environmental health and safety programs
* Conduct risk assessments of work sites to identify potential hazards and formulate plans to mitigate them
* Coordinate with insurance carriers to ensure that appropriate coverage is in place to cover any potential risks
* Review the employee accident reports and medical claims to evaluate the need for potential changes to current policies or procedures
* Consult with engineers to ensure that building designs are safe and compliant with current regulations
* Performs other related duties as required and assigned

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Maintain staff by training employees; maintaining a safe, secure, and legal work environment; developing personal growth opportunities.
* Set objectives, monitor performance, and develop individual training plans to support professional development

* Communicate job expectations; planning, monitoring, and assessing job results; coaching, and counseling employees; developing, coordinating, and enforcing systems, procedures, and productivity standards.
* Establish strategic goals; identifying and evaluating trends; choosing a course of action; defining objectives; evaluating outcomes.
* Set strategic direction and coordinate the work of others to achieve objectives.

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE**

**Minimum Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Safety, Occupational Safety and Health, or related field required; Masters degree desirable.

* Minimum 8 years working experience in Supply Chain environment in Food and Beverage or other perishable goods
* 5+ years of safety and environmental experience in a manufacturing environment. Experience with a union manufacturing environment is a plus.
* Excellent negotiation skills and the ability to influence others while maintaining professionalism
* Proficient in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook (knowledge in Excel should extend past spreadsheet manipulation and should include creation of formulas)
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills
* Detailed oriented and can multi-task
* Excellent time management skills

**Additional Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in the food/beverage industry
* Experience in Manufacturing or production environment
* Experience with risk management and project management
* Must pay high attention to detail and have strong interpersonal, communication, and observation skills
* Experience in report writing
* Proven organizational skills
* Ability to direct, coach, and train others
* Consultative, influential, strategic thinking and problem-solving skills

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS & WORKING CONDITIONS**

This position requires sufficient physical ability to work in a typical office setting; driving a motor vehicle and occasionally working in the field/production setting.

**FREQUENT:** sitting, upward and downward flexion of neck; fine finger dexterity and light to moderate finger pressure to include extended periods of keyboard and mouse use, side-to-side turning of neck, walking, standing, bending and stooping, pushing/pulling, twisting at waist, moderate wrist torque to twist equipment knobs and dials.

**OCCASIONAL:** squatting, kneeling, reach above and at shoulder height, moderate grasp to manipulate reference books and manuals; lifting objects weighing 20 – 35 lbs. from below waist to above shoulders and transporting distances up to 50 feet.

**VISION:** Ability to see in the normal visual range with or without correction.

**HEARING:** Ability to hear in the normal audio range with or without correction.

**This job description is not intended to contain a comprehensive list of the responsibilities that are required to successfully perform in this position. Other duties as assigned are part of every job description. The conditions herein are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals to perform the essential job functions.**

**This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.**

protected_roles.description:
**Overview**

We are seeking an experienced, results-driven **Plant Manager** to lead all daily manufacturing and facility operations. In this role, you will oversee production performance, quality standards, equipment maintenance, and environmental health and safety (EHS/OSHA) compliance. You will manage plant-level budgets, drive improvement initiatives, and build a high-performing, accountable team.

**Responsibilities**

* Provide leadership, coordination, direction and oversight of management/supervisory personnel assigned to power generation facilities.
* Review, analyze, plan, coordinate, and lead all activities within the Operations Department.
* Ensure plant availability and execution of operating and maintenance schedules in conjunction with Plant Staff. • Enforce OSHA, NERC and Environmental permit regulations, investigating accidents, and tracking safety violations.
* Improve processes to optimize asset performance.
* Direct preventive/predictive maintenance programs and coordinate major plant overhauls or planned outages to minimize downtown.
* Establish goals to provide continual improvement in operational productivity and quality.
* Facilitate operational and process engineering changes as necessary.
* Provide oversight to foster an environment that encourages employee involvement.
* Provide guidance and support to ensure safety, environmental, and regulatory compliance.
* Coordinate fulfillment of obligations to its contract counterparties and the energy markets.
* Prepare and manage annual operating and labor budgets, vendor contracts, parts inventory and cost control initiatives.
* Hire, train, schedule and evaluate plant operators, engineers and maintenance staff.
* Ensure compliance with all company standards, practices and policies.
* Oversee the administration of all computerized databases, file systems, and reporting systems for the collection and processing of plant related data.
* Perform other duties as deemed necessary by Owner and VP of Operations.

**Skills**

* A bachelor's degree in business or engineering discipline or equivalent experience preferred.
* A minimum of 10-15 years’ experience in hydroelectric, steam and/or electric power plant operations.
* A minimum of 5 years’ management experience.
* Practical knowledge of power generation systems, boilers, gas turbines, and equipment maintenance.
* Mechanical knowledge, electrical systems familiarity, and engineering troubleshooting ability; technical proficiency with plant equipment and P&IDs.
* Understanding of water and wastewater treatment, pipelines, oil and gas operations, safety regulations, and environmental compliance.
* Readiness to follow emergency response procedures and use PPE and respiratory protection correctly.

**Director of Quality**

**Location**

Carmel, IN • Memphis, TN • St. Louis, MO • Malden, MO • Peoria, IL • Other Illinois locations

**Leadership**

Directly manages at least two quality team members

**Travel**

Regular travel to manufacturing facilities and business locations, as needed

Weaver Popcorn is seeking a seasoned quality leader ready to step into a broader Director-level role. The Director of Quality provides strategic and operational leadership for food safety, quality assurance, regulatory compliance, audit readiness, and continuous improvement across the organization’s food manufacturing operations. This leader will strengthen and standardize quality systems, develop quality talent, and partner with plant and business leaders to ensure products consistently meet company, customer, certification, and regulatory requirements.

This is a hands-on leadership role for an experienced food manufacturing quality professional who can set direction while remaining actively engaged with plant teams, audits, investigations, corrective actions, and day-to-day execution.

**HOW WILL YOU HELP US GROW?**
==============================

**Quality & Food Safety Leadership**
------------------------------------

* Develop and lead the company’s quality and food safety strategy, priorities, policies, procedures, and performance expectations across manufacturing locations.
* Ensure quality assurance and food safety programs are effectively implemented, maintained, verified, and continuously improved.
* Establish and oversee grain and popcorn quality standards from grower receipt and bulk storage through processing, bagging, and shipment, ensuring consistent quality controls throughout the supply chain.
* Provide visible leadership on the manufacturing floor through routine plant engagement, risk reviews, verification activities, and follow-up on quality concerns.
* Build a culture of accountability, prevention, compliance, and continuous improvement across Quality, Operations, Supply Chain, Sales, and other partner functions.

**SQF, Audits & Regulatory Compliance**
---------------------------------------

* Lead and maintain SQF certification programs, including system ownership, audit preparation, certification readiness, corrective actions, and ongoing compliance.
* Plan, lead, and oversee internal, customer, certification, and regulatory audits of food manufacturing facilities.
* Ensure timely closure of audit findings, nonconformances, corrective and preventive actions, and related verification activities.
* Lead cross-functional Food Safety/HACCP, risk assessment, prerequisite program, and food quality teams.
* Monitor applicable food safety and quality requirements and translate them into practical operating standards and controls.
* Ensure effective quality controls for bulk grain storage, bin holds and releases, sampling, testing, and corn disposition prior to processing, including compliance with applicable phytosanitary requirements.

**Quality Management Systems**
------------------------------

* Own the effective use and continuous improvement of quality management system software, including document control, audits, corrective actions, training records, verification, and reporting.
* Standardize quality documentation, specifications, procedures, policies, records, and reporting across facilities.
* Use quality data, trend analysis, and leading and lagging indicators to identify risk, establish priorities, and improve performance.
* Ensure effective controls for ingredient sampling, product verification, environmental monitoring, sanitation verification, traceability, and other core quality programs.
* Provide oversight of corn testing and laboratory quality programs, including mycotoxin testing, internal and third-party sample testing, review of test results, and appropriate product disposition based on quality and food safety requirements.

**People Leadership & Cross-Functional Partnership**
----------------------------------------------------

* Lead, coach, and develop a quality team of at least two direct reports, with potential for broader team responsibility as the function grows.
* Set clear goals, define accountabilities, assess performance, strengthen technical capability, and create development plans for quality team members.
* Partner with Plant Managers and Operations leaders to resolve quality issues without compromising food safety, customer requirements, or regulatory compliance.
* Establish and enforce hold/release and product disposition standards, with authority to stop processing or bagging operations and place grain, ingredients, or finished product on hold when food safety or quality requirements are not met.
* Partner with Sales and Customer Service to respond to customer documentation requests, audits, samples, complaints, and quality-related inquiries.
* Lead investigations into customer complaints, product or process deviations, and recurring issues; ensure root cause analysis and sustainable corrective action.
* Oversee nonconforming material, product holds, rework, release, and disposition processes, partnering with Operations and suppliers to ensure timely resolution and prevent recurrence.
* Provide clear quality updates, risk assessments, recommendations, and performance reporting to senior leadership and other decision-makers.

**WHAT DO YOU NEED TO HAVE?**
=============================

* Bachelor's degree in food science, Food Safety, Microbiology, Chemistry, Biology, Engineering, or related fields.
* 8–10+ years of progressive quality or food safety experience in the food manufacturing industry.
* At least 5 years of people-management experience, including progressive supervisory and manager-level responsibility.
* Proven leadership of SQF certification programs and successful food manufacturing audits.
* Demonstrated knowledge of food safety principles, quality assurance procedures and policies, HACCP-based programs, risk assessment, corrective action, and preventive controls.
* Experience leading internal, customer, certification, and/or regulatory audits across food manufacturing environments.
* Hands-on experience with quality management system software and electronic quality records.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through influence, develop teams, manage competing priorities, and drive consistent execution across locations.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate quality risk and technical requirements to operational and executive audiences.
* Ability to travel regularly to manufacturing facilities and business locations, as needed.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Experience in grain, corn, popcorn, milling, ingredient, or related agricultural processing.
* SQF Practitioner experience and formal training in HACCP, PCQI, internal auditing, root cause analysis, or preventive controls.
* Experience supporting multiple manufacturing sites or standardizing quality systems across locations.
* Experience with supplier quality, customer complaint management, environmental monitoring, traceability, recall readiness, and food defense programs.

**WHAT DOES SUCCESS LOOK LIKE?**
================================

* Consistent audit and certification readiness across facilities.
* Stronger standardization and adoption of quality systems, procedures, and records.
* Timely, well-documented corrective action with verified effectiveness.
* Reduced recurrence of quality issues and customer complaints through disciplined root cause analysis.
* A capable, accountable quality team with clear goals and development plans.
* Credible, practical partnership with Operations and business leaders while maintaining independent quality judgment.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT & SCHEDULE**
===============================

This role operates across office and food manufacturing environments and requires regular presence in production areas. The typical schedule is Monday through Friday; however, the Director of Quality must be available outside normal business hours, including occasional evenings or weekends, when operational, audit, customer, or food safety needs require support. Regular travel is expected based on business needs.

**HOW WILL WE HELP YOU GROW?**
==============================

* Competitive compensation.
* Three weeks of paid time off in the first year.
* 401(k) plan with a company match of 100% of employee deferrals up to 10%.
* Health, vision, dental, life, and disability insurance beginning the first day of the month following 30 days of employment.
* Education reimbursement of up to $15,000 per year.

**EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY**
================================

Weaver Popcorn is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and associates. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without regard to any status protected by applicable law.

*The role responsibilities are many, various, and not limited to those written in this document*

protected_roles.title: Plant/Manufacturing Director
protected_roles.description:
Job Summary
 
Maker’s Pride is seeking a proven, enterprise-minded Plant Director to lead our largest manufacturing facility in McComb, Ohio, a site of more than 1,600 Team Members that is critical to the success of our business. The Plant Director holds full accountability for the safety, quality, service, cost, and people performance of a large-scale co-manufacturing operation, and serves as the senior leader on site and the face of the plant to customers, Team Members, and the community.
 
This role requires a seasoned operations executive who has led large, complex plants of 1,000+ Team Members, can build and develop a strong leadership bench, and can balance day-to-day execution with long-term strategy. The Plant Director partners closely with senior leadership and corporate functions to deliver the plant’s operating plan, drive operational excellence, and position McComb for sustained growth.
 
 
Key Responsibilities
 

* Operational Leadership: Lead all plant operations, including production, packaging, maintenance, engineering, quality, warehouse, and supply chain, to consistently deliver safety, quality, service, and cost targets across multiple shifts and lines.
* P&L and Financial Accountability: Own the plant’s operating plan, budget, and financial performance, including labor, overtime, yield, waste, and capital spend. Identify and execute cost-reduction and margin-improvement opportunities.
* Strategic Planning: Develop and execute a multi-year plant strategy aligned to enterprise goals, covering capacity, capital investment, automation, new business onboarding, and talent.
* Production Planning and Capacity: Partner with Supply Chain, Planning, and Customer teams to build production schedules and resource plans that optimize throughput, labor utilization, and on-time, in-full performance.
* Quality and Food Safety: Ensure strict adherence to quality, food safety, and regulatory requirements (e.g., FDA, GMP, HACCP, and customer and third-party audit standards). Drive corrective and preventive actions and maintain audit readiness at all times.
* Safety Culture: Champion a zero-harm culture. Enforce safety policies, lead regular audits and incident reviews, and hold the leadership team accountable for proactive hazard prevention and compliance.
* Workforce Strategy and Labor Relations: Partner with HR to attract, retain, and engage a large and diverse workforce. Drive staffing stability, reduce turnover, manage overtime effectively, and foster positive Team Member and labor relations, including compliance with applicable employment and labor laws and agreements.
* Customer and Partner Relationships: Serve as the senior site representative with co-manufacturing customers, hosting visits and audits, resolving escalations, and building long-term trust. Collaborate with suppliers to ensure timely delivery of materials and finished goods.
* Continuous Improvement: Lead a data-driven operational excellence program using Lean, Six Sigma, or similar methodologies to eliminate waste, improve OEE and yield, and standardize best practices across shifts.
* Capital and Asset Management: Oversee capital planning, project execution, and asset reliability to ensure equipment, infrastructure, and facilities support safe, efficient, and scalable operations.
* Reporting and Executive Communication: Provide regular, transparent reporting on safety, quality, production, financial, and workforce KPIs to senior leadership, with clear analysis, risks, and recommendations.
* Community and Site Presence: Represent Maker’s Pride in the McComb community and maintain a visible, accessible leadership presence on the plant floor across all shifts.

Supervisory Responsibilities
 

* Leadership of a Large Organization: Provide direct leadership to the plant leadership team and overall leadership of 1,600+ Team Members, including managers, supervisors, technicians, and support staff.
* Talent Development: Build a strong leadership bench through coaching, performance management, succession planning, and development of high-potential leaders.
* Culture and Accountability: Foster a culture of safety, quality, teamwork, accountability, respect, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications
 

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field required; Master’s degree or MBA preferred.
* Experience: 15+ years of progressive manufacturing operations experience, including 7+ years in a senior plant leadership role (Plant Manager, Plant Director, or equivalent).
* Scale: Demonstrated success leading large, complex, multi-shift plants of 1,000+ Team Members, with full P&L accountability.
* Industry: Experience in co-manufacturing, food, beverage, or other high-volume, regulated manufacturing environments strongly preferred.
* Operational Excellence: Track record of delivering measurable improvements in safety, quality, productivity, and cost. Lean, Six Sigma, or similar certification desirable.
* Workforce Leadership: Proven ability to lead, motivate, and develop a large, diverse workforce, including strong experience with staffing, retention, and employee and labor relations. Experience in a unionized environment is a plus.
* Regulatory Knowledge: Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, food safety and quality standards, and regulatory requirements.
* Technology: Proficiency in ERP systems and Microsoft Office Suite; experience with manufacturing software (e.g., SAP, Oracle) is a plus.
* Leadership Skills: Strategic thinker with excellent executive presence, communication, and decision-making skills; able to influence at all levels of the organization and with customers.
* Analytical Skills: Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities with a focus on data-driven decision-making.

The information provided in this document provides an overview of the most common duties, qualifications, and demands of the position. It is not intended to be a comprehensive summary of the role, and the duties, qualifications, and demands of the position are subject to change without notice. The expectations provided here may also be modified if an employee with a disability could effectively meet the expectations for the role with reasonable accommodation.

The Director of Manufacturing executes the company operating plan within capital and operating budget parameters. The Director of Manufacturing works with the executive leadership team to develop strategies and objectives to maximize productivity and profitability. Analyzes production trends, forecasts future requirements, solve problems, motivates & develops employees.

* Ensure consistency in collective bargaining agreement and provide support during contract negotiations
* Effect necessary communication and motivation to staff. Monitors individual performance via observation and review of various productivity measures. Counsels and disciplines as necessary.
* Provides production required safety leadership and training and is responsible for improved safety performance
* Oversees all production planning and executing against demand signals.
* Oversees facility maintenance team, including Cap-Ex planning and execution.
* Provides input on new product development.
* Ensure compliance with all appropriate health and food safety regulations and cleanliness, including audit preparation

protected_roles.title: Global Director of Quality
protected_roles.description:
**Lead Globally. Drive Innovation. Make an Impact.**

**Join Amphenol Alden and Make a Difference in Patient Care Worldwide!**

At **Amphenol Alden Products (AAP)**, what we do matters. Our medical cable assemblies and interconnect solutions support the advanced technologies healthcare professionals rely on every day. Behind every product is a patient, a family, and an opportunity to make a difference in someone's life.

With roots as a family business more than 90 years ago, Amphenol Alden combines a proud history and entrepreneurial spirit with the resources and opportunities of a global corporation. We are a growing organization that values innovation, teamwork, accountability, and the contributions of our employees.

We believe our people are the foundation of our success. That's why we offer competitive compensation, an outstanding benefits package, work/life balance, and opportunities for professional growth and development.

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking an experienced and strategic **Global Director of Quality** to lead and advance quality operations across four manufacturing facilities in the United States, Mexico, India, and China.

Reporting to AAP’s General Manager and serving as a member of the Leadership Team, this individual will establish and drive the global quality strategy, strengthen Quality Management Systems (QMS), and promote a culture of quality excellence and continuous improvement throughout the organization.

This is an opportunity to make a significant impact by developing high-performing global Quality teams, driving operational improvements, strengthening customer and supplier partnerships, and ensuring consistent quality standards across all manufacturing locations.

**Principal Duties and Responsibilities**

* **Global Quality Strategy:** Develop and execute global quality strategies, objectives, and initiatives that support business goals, product quality, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence.
* **Quality Management Systems:** Lead the development, implementation, standardization, and continuous improvement of Quality Management Systems across all facilities, ensuring compliance with ISO 9001, ISO 13485, applicable FDA requirements, customer specifications, and other relevant regulatory standards.
* **Executive Leadership:** Participate as a member of the Executive Leadership Team in establishing business strategies, operational objectives, and organizational improvement initiatives.
* **Quality Performance:** Establish and monitor global quality metrics, including customer complaints, internal and supplier defects, Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ), corrective actions, and audit performance. Drive measurable improvements in quality and process capability.
* **Continuous Improvement:** Champion Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and data-driven problem-solving methodologies to reduce defects, minimize waste, improve process consistency, and enhance overall operational performance.
* **Engineering and Operations Partnership:** Collaborate with Engineering and Operations to ensure effective quality planning, design and process FMEAs, risk assessments, process validation, and verification throughout the product lifecycle.
* **New Product Introduction:** Provide quality leadership for New Product Introduction (NPI) and manufacturing transfers, ensuring process capability, quality requirements, and customer expectations are met before production release.
* **Supplier Quality:** Partner with Global Supply Chain to develop and maintain a high-performing supplier base through supplier qualification, audits, performance monitoring, development, and corrective action programs.
* **Customer Quality:** Provide strategic leadership for customer quality initiatives, serving as the senior escalation point for significant quality concerns, customer audits, and corrective action resolution.
* **Audits and Regulatory Compliance:** Oversee internal and external quality audits, regulatory inspections, and management reviews, ensuring findings are addressed promptly and compliance is sustained.
* **Corrective and Preventive Action:** Strengthen global CAPA processes through effective root cause analysis, risk mitigation, and prevention of recurring quality issues.
* **Global Team Leadership:** Lead, mentor, and develop the global Quality organization, establishing clear expectations, accountability, talent development plans, and succession strategies.
* **Global Standardization:** Promote consistency and the sharing of best practices across manufacturing facilities in the United States, Mexico, India, and China.
* **Executive Reporting:** Provide regular updates to executive leadership on global quality performance, emerging risks, customer satisfaction, and progress toward strategic quality objectives.

**Related Experience and Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Quality, Engineering, or a related technical or scientific discipline; Master's degree preferred.
* 10+ years of previous related experience and at least 5 years of experience managing individuals.
* Strong knowledge of ISO 13485, ISO 9001, FDA Quality System requirements, and applicable regulatory standards.
* Demonstrated experience leading Quality Management Systems and continuous improvement initiatives across multiple manufacturing locations.
* Strong working knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, CAPA, root cause analysis, risk management, and quality improvement methodologies.
* Proven ability to influence cross-functional teams, develop talent, and drive results in a global organization.

protected_roles.title: Head of Quality
protected_roles.description:
**About Tutor**

We believe robots should be the next chapter in making physical labor safer and more affordable. But, nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t have a single robot. Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

We build robots that go straight into real factories and warehouses, to do real work, with real impact. Our robot Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Our robot Sonny does handwork, using two arms to achieve human-like dexterity in picking and packing. Every robot learns on the job, and each one we deploy makes the next one more capable, more affordable, and faster to put to work.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, we do it all in-house: the robotics hardware, the machine learning, and the field deployment and service. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

**Why Tutor?**

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

**The Role**

Tutor is hiring a Head of Quality to lead quality as a function, alongside the Head of Manufacturing. You own the quality system, supplier quality across our supply base, product safety certifications, and the quality targets the company holds itself to. The quality engineers and the quality manager report to you, and you grow the team from there. You report to the CTO. As our operations organization grows, you and the Head of Manufacturing will report to the leader of that organization.

This is a building role. The first pieces, incoming inspection, supplier controls and failure analysis, are being put in place by the team you will lead. Your job is to turn them into a system that holds as production grows, a supplier base we can trust, and a quality record that customers and certifying bodies can verify. You have the authority to hold any shipment that is not right.

### **Requirements**

* You have led a quality function at a company that builds complex electromechanical hardware in volume
* You have built or rebuilt a quality system and taken it through ISO 9001 or an equivalent certification
* You have run supplier quality across a supply base, including suppliers overseas
* You have taken a product through product safety certification
* You have built and led a team of quality engineers and managers
* You make decisions from data, and you can hold a shipment when the data says so

### **Nice to haves**

* Robotics, automation, vehicles, or capital equipment
* Reliability engineering methods: life testing, failure rate analysis, design reviews
* Building quality data and tooling that other teams use
* Experience with manufacturing execution systems

### **Benefits**

* **Fully employer-covered health insurance**, so you’re protected without the premium.
* **A managed 401(k)** to help you plan for the future.
* **Generous time off:** unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
* **Regular in-office meals** and team social events throughout the year.

**Compensation**

The base salary range for this role is $220,000 to $280,000, depending on experience.

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

*Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.*
